- For a Lipschitz u, its non-differentiability set N_u is Borel and Lⁿ-null (measurableSet_of_differentiableAt, LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt). Du is Borel and bounded (measurable_fderiv, norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz).
- One-variable FTC: a Lipschitz φ : ℝ → ℝ satisfies φ(b) − φ(a) = ∫_a^b deriv φ (LipschitzOnWith.absolutelyContinuousOnInterval and AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval.integral_deriv_eq_sub). If φ(τ) = u(p + τv) and u is differentiable at p + τv, then deriv φ(τ) = Du(p + τv)v.

1. (FTC along translations.) Let u be Lipschitz and z ∈ ℝⁿ. Then for a.e. p ∈ ℝⁿ, u(p + z) − u(p) = ∫_0^1 Du(p + τz)z dτ.
Proof: {(p, τ) ∈ ℝⁿ × [0, 1] : p + τz ∈ N_u} is Borel with null p-sections N_u − τz. By Tonelli, for a.e. p its τ-section is null, and the one-variable FTC applies to τ ↦ u(p + τz).

2. (Interior mollification.) Let ρ̂(z) := c₁(1 − |z|)₊ with c₁ := (∫(1 − |z|)₊ dz)^{−1}.
- ρ̂ ≥ 0, ρ̂ = 0 off B̆_1(0), ∫ρ̂ = 1, sup ρ̂ = c₁, and ρ̂ is c₁-Lipschitz.
- For ε > 0 put ρ̂_ε(w) := ε^{−n}ρ̂(w/ε). It vanishes off B̆_ε(0), has supremum ε^{−n}c₁ and Lipschitz constant ε^{−n−1}c₁.
- For a Lipschitz u let u_ε(x) := ∫ u(x − εz)ρ̂(z) dz = ∫ u(y)ρ̂_ε(x − y) dy.
(2a) If 0 < ε ≤ s ≤ 1/2 then ∫_{B_{1−s}} (u − u_ε)² ≤ ε²∫_B ‖Du‖².
- For x ∈ B_{1−s}, u(x) − u_ε(x) = ∫ (u(x) − u(x − εz))ρ̂(z) dz.
- By step 1 (vector εz, base point p = x − εz; translations preserve null sets) and Tonelli in (x, z), for a.e. x and a.e. z with |z| < 1:
  |u(x) − u(x − εz)| = |∫_0^1 Du(x − εz + τεz)(εz) dτ| ≤ ε∫_0^1 ‖Du(x − (1 − τ)εz)‖ dτ.
- ρ̂(z)dz ⊗ dτ is a probability measure on B̆_1(0) × [0, 1]. So by Jensen, for a.e. x ∈ B_{1−s}:
  (u(x) − u_ε(x))² ≤ ε²∫ρ̂(z)∫_0^1 ‖Du(x − (1 − τ)εz)‖² dτ dz.
- Integrate over x ∈ B_{1−s} and use Tonelli. For each (z, τ) the translation x ↦ x − (1 − τ)εz maps B_{1−s} into B, because |(1 − τ)εz| < ε ≤ s. So ∫_{B_{1−s}} ‖Du(x − (1 − τ)εz)‖² dx ≤ ∫_B ‖Du‖², and (2a) follows.
(2b) Let 0 < ε ≤ s/2 ≤ 1/4 and x, x' ∈ K_s. Then B̆_ε(x) ∪ B̆_ε(x') ⊆ B, since 1 − s + s/2 < 1, and
- |u_ε(x)| ≤ ε^{−n}c₁∫_B |u| ≤ ε^{−n}c₁(ω∫_B u²)^{1/2};
- |u_ε(x) − u_ε(x')| ≤ ε^{−n−1}c₁|x − x'|∫_B |u| ≤ ε^{−n−1}c₁(ω∫_B u²)^{1/2}|x − x'|.

3. (Boundary layer.) For 0 < s ≤ 1/2 and Lipschitz u: ∫_{A_s} u² ≤ 2^{n+3}s(∫_B u² + ∫_B ‖Du‖²).
(i) {(x, σ) ∈ ℝⁿ × [1/2, 1] : σx ∈ N_u} is Borel with null x-sections σ^{−1}N_u. So for a.e. x, u is differentiable at σx for a.e. σ ∈ [1/2, 1]. For such x and every t ∈ [1/2, 1], the one-variable FTC for σ ↦ u(σx) gives u(x) − u(tx) = ∫_t^1 Du(σx)x dσ.
(ii) For such x ∈ A_s (so |x| < 1): |u(x)| ≤ |u(tx)| + ∫_{1/2}^1 ‖Du(σx)‖ dσ. Hence, by Cauchy–Schwarz on an interval of length 1/2,
u(x)² ≤ 2u(tx)² + 2(∫_{1/2}^1 ‖Du(σx)‖ dσ)² ≤ 2u(tx)² + ∫_{1/2}^1 ‖Du(σx)‖² dσ.
Averaging over t ∈ [1/2, 1]: u(x)² ≤ 4∫_{1/2}^1 u(tx)² dt + ∫_{1/2}^1 ‖Du(σx)‖² dσ.
(iii) Integrate over x ∈ A_s (Tonelli): ∫_{A_s} u² ≤ 4∫_{1/2}^1∫_{A_s} u(tx)² dx dt + ∫_{1/2}^1∫_{A_s} ‖Du(σx)‖² dx dσ.
(iv) Let F ≥ 0 be measurable and t ∈ [1/2, 1]. Then ∫_{A_s} F(tx) dx = t^{−n}∫_{tA_s} F ≤ 2ⁿ∫_B F·1_{tA_s}, where tA_s = {y : t(1 − s) ≤ |y| < t} ⊆ B.
By Tonelli, ∫_{1/2}^1∫_{A_s} F(tx) dx dt ≤ 2ⁿ∫_B F(y)ℓ(y) dy, where ℓ(y) := L¹{t ∈ [1/2, 1] : |y| < t ≤ |y|/(1 − s)} ≤ |y|s/(1 − s) ≤ 2s.
Hence ∫_{1/2}^1∫_{A_s} F(tx) dx dt ≤ 2^{n+1}s∫_B F.
(v) Apply (iv) with F = u² and with F = ‖Du‖²: ∫_{A_s} u² ≤ 4·2^{n+1}s∫_B u² + 2^{n+1}s∫_B ‖Du‖² ≤ 2^{n+3}s(∫_B u² + ∫_B ‖Du‖²).

4. (Total boundedness.) Let 𝓛 := Lp ℝ 2 (volume.restrict B), a complete metric space. Let f_j ∈ 𝓛 be the class of u_j; it is in L² because u_j is continuous and bounded on B. Fix η > 0.
- Choose s ∈ (0, 1/2] with 2^{n+3}s·2M ≤ η²/16, and ε ∈ (0, s/2] with ε²M ≤ η²/16.
- By step 3, ‖u_j‖_{L²(A_s)} ≤ η/4 for all j. By (2a), ‖u_j − (u_j)_ε‖_{L²(B_{1−s})} ≤ η/4 for all j.
- By (2b), the restrictions v_j := (u_j)_ε|_{K_s} to the compact set K_s are uniformly bounded and uniformly Lipschitz, hence equicontinuous. By the Arzelà–Ascoli theorem (BoundedContinuousFunction.arzela_ascoli on the compact space K_s), {v_j} is relatively compact, hence totally bounded, for the sup distance.
- So there are indices j_1, …, j_m such that every j has some k with sup_{K_s}|v_j − v_{j_k}| ≤ η/(4√ω).
- Since B = B_{1−s} ∪ A_s and B_{1−s} ⊆ K_s:
  ‖f_j − f_{j_k}‖_𝓛 ≤ ‖u_j‖_{L²(A_s)} + ‖u_{j_k}‖_{L²(A_s)} + ‖u_j − v_j‖_{L²(B_{1−s})} + √ω·sup_{K_s}|v_j − v_{j_k}| + ‖v_{j_k} − u_{j_k}‖_{L²(B_{1−s})} ≤ 5η/4.
η > 0 was arbitrary, so {f_j : j ∈ ℕ} is totally bounded in 𝓛.

5. (Extraction.) In the complete space 𝓛, the closure of a totally bounded set is totally bounded and closed, hence compact (TotallyBounded.closure, TotallyBounded.isCompact_of_isClosed). By IsCompact.tendsto_subseq there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and F ∈ 𝓛 with f_{φ(j)} → F in 𝓛. Let W : ℝⁿ → ℝ be a representative of F, so MemLp W 2 (volume.restrict B). Then ∫_B (u_{φ(j)} − W)² = ‖f_{φ(j)} − F‖²_𝓛 → 0. ∎

Lemma EL (lower semicontinuity of the Dirichlet energy). Let n ≥ 1, R > 0, B := B̆_R(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ (ℝⁿ = Euclid n), and E ∈ ℝ. Let (u_j)_{j∈ℕ} be Lipschitz functions ℝⁿ → ℝ with ∫_B ‖Du_j‖² ≤ E for all j, (c_j)_{j∈ℕ} real numbers, W : ℝⁿ → ℝ with W ∈ L²(B) and ∫_B (u_j − c_j − W)² → 0, and h : ℝⁿ → ℝ of class C² on B with h = W Lⁿ-almost everywhere on B (D = fderiv ℝ, operator norm). Then ‖Dh‖² is integrable on B and ∫_B ‖Dh‖² ≤ E.
Proof of Lemma EL.
Source: in the Lipschitz/L² setting of the frozen statements, this replaces one step of Simon's proof of Lemma 5.3.1: "∇f_{k'} ⇀ ∇w weakly in L², with ∫_B|∇w|² ≤ 1" (weak lower semicontinuity of the Dirichlet energy). The proof is by duality against compactly supported C¹ vector fields.

Notation.
- B := B̆_R(0), and e_i is the standard basis.
- For a vector field Φ = (Φ_1, …, Φ_n): divΦ := Σ_i ∂_iΦ_i and |Φ|² := Σ_i Φ_i².
- For u differentiable at y: ∇u·Φ(y) := Σ_i Du(y)(e_i)Φ_i(y). By Cauchy–Schwarz, |∇u·Φ| ≤ ‖Du(y)‖·|Φ(y)|, since the operator norm ‖Du(y)‖ is the Euclidean length of the gradient.
- 𝒱 is the set of Φ whose components are C¹ on ℝⁿ with compact support and tsupport Φ_i ⊆ B.

0. E ≥ 0, because E ≥ ∫_B ‖Du_0‖² ≥ 0.

1. (IBP for Lipschitz functions.) If u is Lipschitz and Φ ∈ 𝒱, then ∫_B ∇u·Φ = −∫_B u·divΦ and ∫_B divΦ = 0.
Proof: each Φ_i is C¹ with compact support, hence Lipschitz (ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport). LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq with f := u, g := Φ_i, v := e_i gives
∫ lineDeriv ℝ u y e_i·Φ_i(y) dy = ∫ lineDeriv ℝ Φ_i y (−e_i)·u(y) dy = −∫ ∂_iΦ_i(y)·u(y) dy.
By Rademacher (LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt), for a.e. y, u is differentiable at y and lineDeriv ℝ u y e_i = Du(y)e_i. Sum over i. All integrands vanish outside ⋃_i tsupport Φ_i ⊆ B, so the integrals over ℝⁿ equal those over B. Taking u ≡ 1 (Du = 0) gives ∫_B divΦ = 0.

2. (IBP for h.) If Φ ∈ 𝒱 then ∫_B ∇h·Φ = −∫_B h·divΦ.
Proof:
- K := ⋃_i tsupport Φ_i is a compact subset of B, so K ⊆ closedBall(0, r₁) for some r₁ < R.
- Choose χ ∈ C^∞(ℝⁿ) with χ ≡ 1 on B̆_{r₂}(0) and tsupport χ ⊆ closedBall(0, r₃), where r₁ < r₂ < r₃ < R (a ContDiffBump).
- Put h̃ := χh on B and h̃ := 0 off B. Then h̃ is C² on ℝⁿ (C² on B, and zero on the open set ℝⁿ ∖ tsupport χ), has compact support, is Lipschitz, and is differentiable everywhere.
- The computation of step 1 with u := h̃ gives ∫ ∇h̃·Φ = −∫ h̃·divΦ. On the open set B̆_{r₂}(0) ⊇ K we have h̃ = h and Dh̃ = Dh, and both integrands vanish off K.

3. (Duality bound.) For Φ ∈ 𝒱: ∫_B ∇h·Φ ≤ √E·(∫_B |Φ|²)^{1/2}.
Proof:
- By step 2 and h = W a.e. on B, ∫_B ∇h·Φ = −∫_B W·divΦ.
- divΦ is bounded and supported in B, so by Cauchy–Schwarz |∫_B (u_j − c_j − W)·divΦ| ≤ (∫_B (u_j − c_j − W)²)^{1/2}(∫_B (divΦ)²)^{1/2} → 0.
- Hence −∫_B W·divΦ = lim_j −∫_B (u_j − c_j)·divΦ = lim_j −∫_B u_j·divΦ = lim_j ∫_B ∇u_j·Φ, using step 1 and ∫_B divΦ = 0.
- For every j, |∫_B ∇u_j·Φ| ≤ ∫_B ‖Du_j‖·|Φ| ≤ (∫_B ‖Du_j‖²)^{1/2}(∫_B |Φ|²)^{1/2} ≤ √E·(∫_B |Φ|²)^{1/2}. The bound passes to the limit.

4. (Energy on interior balls.) Let 0 < r < R.
- Choose χ_r ∈ C^∞(ℝⁿ) with 0 ≤ χ_r ≤ 1, χ_r ≡ 1 on B̆_r(0) and tsupport χ_r ⊆ closedBall(0, (r + R)/2) ⊆ B (a ContDiffBump centred at 0 with rIn = r, rOut = (r + R)/2).
- Put Φ_i := χ_r·∂_ih on B and Φ_i := 0 off B. Since h is C² on B, Φ_i is C¹ on B and vanishes on the open set ℝⁿ ∖ tsupport χ_r. So Φ ∈ 𝒱.
- ∇h·Φ = χ_r‖Dh‖² and |Φ|² = χ_r²‖Dh‖² ≤ χ_r‖Dh‖².
- Let X := ∫_B χ_r‖Dh‖². It is finite, because the integrand is continuous with compact support in B.
- Step 3 gives X ≤ √E·√X, hence X ≤ E (trivial if X = 0; otherwise divide by √X).
- Since χ_r = 1 on B̆_r(0) and the integrand is ≥ 0, ∫_{B̆_r(0)} ‖Dh‖² ≤ X ≤ E.

5. (Exhaustion.) ‖Dh‖² is continuous on B, hence a.e.-strongly measurable for volume.restrict B. Take r_k := R(1 − 1/(k + 1)) ↑ R. By monotone convergence for lower integrals, ∫⁻_B ‖Dh‖² = lim_k ∫⁻_{B̆_{r_k}(0)} ‖Dh‖² ≤ E < ∞. Hence ‖Dh‖² is integrable on B and ∫_B ‖Dh‖² ≤ E. ∎

Lemma HA (harmonic approximation; Simon 3.1). For every n ≥ 1 and every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 with the following property. Let R₀ > 0 and let w : ℝⁿ → ℝ (ℝⁿ = Euclid n) be Lipschitz with ∫_{B̆_{R₀}(0)} ‖Dw‖² ≤ R₀ⁿ and |∫_{B̆_{R₀}(0)} Σ_i ∂_iw·∂_iζ| ≤ δR₀ⁿG for every C¹ compactly supported ζ : ℝⁿ → ℝ with tsupport ζ ⊆ B̆_{R₀}(0) and every G ∈ ℝ with ‖Dζ(v)‖ ≤ G for all v (Dw = fderiv ℝ w, ∂_iw = Dw(e_i), e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1). Then there is h : ℝⁿ → ℝ such that: h is C^m on B̆_{R₀}(0) for every m ∈ ℕ; Σ_i iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 h y ![e_i, e_i] = 0 for every y ∈ B̆_{R₀}(0); ‖Dh‖² is integrable on B̆_{R₀}(0) with ∫_{B̆_{R₀}(0)} ‖Dh‖² ≤ R₀ⁿ; and (h − w)² is integrable on B̆_{R₀}(0) with ∫_{B̆_{R₀}(0)} (h − w)² ≤ εR₀^{n+2}.
Proof of Lemma HA.
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 5, Lemma 3.1 (Harmonic Approximation Lemma) and its printed proof, first for the unit ball (Part A below), then rescaled (Part B below). W^{1,2} is unavailable in the frozen Lean setting, so the proof is adapted as follows:
- the f_k are Lipschitz;
- the harmonicity of the L² limit comes from the distributional identity ∫WΔζ = 0 and Lemma WL, instead of from weak convergence of gradients;
- the energy bound for the limit comes from Lemma EL, instead of weak lower semicontinuity.
Lemmas used: PI (constant C_P), RC, WL and EL above.

Notation.
- B_ρ := B̆_ρ(0) and ω := Lⁿ(B_1).
- For Lipschitz u and C¹ ζ, ∇u·∇ζ := Σ_i Du(e_i)·Dζ(e_i). This is exactly the Lean integrand Σ_i fderiv ℝ u v (e_i) * fderiv ℝ ζ v (e_i).
- Δζ := Σ_i D²ζ(e_i, e_i) with D²ζ(y)(a, b) = iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 ζ y ![a, b].
- H(w, R₀, δ) is the hypothesis of the statement: for every C¹ compactly supported ζ with tsupport ζ ⊆ B_{R₀} and every G with ‖Dζ(v)‖ ≤ G for all v, |∫_{B_{R₀}} ∇w·∇ζ| ≤ δR₀ⁿG.
- "h is admissible for (w, R₀, ε)" means: h is C^m on B_{R₀} for every m ∈ ℕ; Δh = 0 on B_{R₀}; ‖Dh‖² is integrable on B_{R₀} with ∫_{B_{R₀}} ‖Dh‖² ≤ R₀ⁿ; and (h − w)² is integrable on B_{R₀} with ∫_{B_{R₀}} (h − w)² ≤ εR₀^{n+2}.

Step 0 (integration by parts). Let u be Lipschitz and ζ ∈ C²(ℝⁿ) with compact support and tsupport ζ ⊆ B_1. Then ∫_{B_1} ∇u·∇ζ = −∫_{B_1} u·Δζ and ∫_{B_1} Δζ = 0.
Proof:
- g_i := Dζ(·)e_i is C¹ with compact support, hence Lipschitz.
- LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq with f := u, g := g_i, v := e_i gives ∫ lineDeriv ℝ u y e_i·g_i(y) dy = ∫ lineDeriv ℝ g_i y (−e_i)·u(y) dy = −∫ Dg_i(y)(e_i)·u(y) dy, and Dg_i(y)(e_i) = D²ζ(y)(e_i, e_i) (iteratedFDeriv_two_apply).
- For a.e. y, u is differentiable at y (Rademacher) and lineDeriv ℝ u y e_i = Du(y)e_i.
- Summing over i gives the first identity on ℝⁿ, and both integrands vanish outside tsupport ζ ⊆ B_1. With u ≡ 1 we get ∫_{B_1} Δζ = 0.

Part A (R₀ = 1). Claim A: for every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 such that every Lipschitz w with ∫_{B_1} ‖Dw‖² ≤ 1 and H(w, 1, δ) has an admissible h for (w, 1, ε).
A1. Suppose Claim A fails for some ε > 0. Then for each j ∈ ℕ, taking δ := 1/(j + 1), there is a Lipschitz w_j with ∫_{B_1} ‖Dw_j‖² ≤ 1 and H(w_j, 1, 1/(j + 1)) for which no admissible h for (w_j, 1, ε) exists.
A2. Let λ_j := ω^{−1}∫_{B_1} w_j and u_j := w_j − λ_j. Then u_j is Lipschitz and Du_j = Dw_j.
- By Lemma PI, ∫_{B_1} u_j² ≤ C_P∫_{B_1} ‖Dw_j‖² ≤ C_P.
- With M := max(C_P, 1), Lemma RC applies to (u_j). It gives a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and W with MemLp W 2 on B_1 and ∫_{B_1} (u_{φ(j)} − W)² → 0.
A3. Let ζ ∈ C²(ℝⁿ) with compact support and tsupport ζ ⊆ B_1.
- ζ is C¹, and Dζ is continuous with compact support, so G_ζ := sup_v ‖Dζ(v)‖ < ∞.
- H(w_k, 1, 1/(k + 1)) with G = G_ζ gives |∫_{B_1} ∇w_k·∇ζ| ≤ G_ζ/(k + 1).
- By Step 0, ∫_{B_1} u_k·Δζ = ∫_{B_1} w_k·Δζ − λ_k∫_{B_1} Δζ = −∫_{B_1} ∇w_k·∇ζ. Hence |∫_{B_1} u_{φ(j)}·Δζ| ≤ G_ζ/(φ(j) + 1) → 0.
- Δζ is bounded, so by Cauchy–Schwarz |∫_{B_1} (u_{φ(j)} − W)·Δζ| ≤ (∫_{B_1} (u_{φ(j)} − W)²)^{1/2}(∫_{B_1} (Δζ)²)^{1/2} → 0.
- Therefore ∫_{B_1} W·Δζ = 0.
W is integrable on B_1 (it is L² on a set of finite measure). So Lemma WL with R = 1 gives h̃ that is C^m on B_1 for every m, with Δh̃ = 0 on B_1 and h̃ = W a.e. on B_1.
A4. Apply Lemma EL with R = 1, E = 1, the Lipschitz functions w_{φ(j)}, the constants c_j := λ_{φ(j)}, the function W, and h := h̃ (C² on B_1). Its hypotheses hold: ∫_{B_1} ‖Dw_{φ(j)}‖² ≤ 1, and ∫_{B_1} (w_{φ(j)} − λ_{φ(j)} − W)² = ∫_{B_1} (u_{φ(j)} − W)² → 0. Hence ‖Dh̃‖² is integrable on B_1 and ∫_{B_1} ‖Dh̃‖² ≤ 1.
A5. Choose j with ∫_{B_1} (u_{φ(j)} − W)² ≤ ε, and put h := h̃ + λ_{φ(j)}.
- Adding a constant changes no derivative of order ≥ 1. So on B_1, h is C^m for every m, Dh = Dh̃, D²h = D²h̃, Δh = 0, and ‖Dh‖² is integrable with ∫_{B_1} ‖Dh‖² ≤ 1 = 1ⁿ.
- A.e. on B_1, h − w_{φ(j)} = h̃ − u_{φ(j)} = W − u_{φ(j)}. So (h − w_{φ(j)})² is integrable on B_1 (W ∈ L² and u_{φ(j)} is bounded on B_1), and ∫_{B_1} (h − w_{φ(j)})² ≤ ε = ε·1^{n+2}.
Thus h is admissible for (w_{φ(j)}, 1, ε), contradicting A1 for the index φ(j). This proves Claim A.

Part B (scaling). Given ε > 0, let δ be the constant of Claim A for this ε. Let R₀ > 0 and let w be Lipschitz with ∫_{B_{R₀}} ‖Dw‖² ≤ R₀ⁿ and H(w, R₀, δ).
B1. Put w₁(y) := R₀^{−1}w(R₀y). It is Lipschitz.
- Dw₁(y) = Dw(R₀y) for every y. If w is differentiable at R₀y this is the chain rule. Otherwise w₁ is not differentiable at y either, because w = R₀w₁(·/R₀), and both fderivs are 0.
- Change of variables x = R₀y: Measure.setIntegral_comp_smul_of_pos with finrank = n and R₀·B_1 = B_{R₀} (and Measure.map_addHaar_smul for lower integrals) give ∫_{B_1} F(R₀y) dy = R₀^{−n}∫_{B_{R₀}} F for F integrable on B_{R₀} or F ≥ 0 measurable. Integrability transfers in both directions.
- So ∫_{B_1} ‖Dw₁‖² = R₀^{−n}∫_{B_{R₀}} ‖Dw‖² ≤ 1.
B2. H(w₁, 1, δ) holds. Let ζ₁ be C¹ with compact support and tsupport ζ₁ ⊆ B_1, and let G satisfy ‖Dζ₁(v)‖ ≤ G for all v.
- Put ζ(x) := R₀ζ₁(x/R₀). ζ is C¹ with compact support, tsupport ζ = R₀·tsupport ζ₁ ⊆ B_{R₀}, and Dζ(x) = Dζ₁(x/R₀), so ‖Dζ(x)‖ ≤ G.
- By H(w, R₀, δ), |∫_{B_{R₀}} ∇w·∇ζ| ≤ δR₀ⁿG.
- By B1 and the change of variables, ∫_{B_{R₀}} ∇w·∇ζ = ∫_{B_{R₀}} Σ_i Dw(x)e_i·Dζ₁(x/R₀)e_i dx = R₀ⁿ∫_{B_1} Σ_i Dw(R₀y)e_i·Dζ₁(y)e_i dy = R₀ⁿ∫_{B_1} ∇w₁·∇ζ₁.
Hence |∫_{B_1} ∇w₁·∇ζ₁| ≤ δG.
B3. By Claim A there is h₁ admissible for (w₁, 1, ε). Put h(x) := R₀h₁(x/R₀).
- h is C^m on B_{R₀} for every m, since x ↦ x/R₀ is linear and maps B_{R₀} onto B_1.
- Dh(x) = Dh₁(x/R₀) and D²h(x)(a, b) = R₀^{−1}D²h₁(x/R₀)(a, b). So Δh(x) = R₀^{−1}Δh₁(x/R₀) = 0 on B_{R₀}.
- By the change of variables of B1, ‖Dh‖² is integrable on B_{R₀} and ∫_{B_{R₀}} ‖Dh‖² = R₀ⁿ∫_{B_1} ‖Dh₁‖² ≤ R₀ⁿ.
- Since h(x) − w(x) = R₀(h₁ − w₁)(x/R₀), (h − w)² is integrable on B_{R₀} and ∫_{B_{R₀}} (h − w)² = R₀²·R₀ⁿ∫_{B_1} (h₁ − w₁)² ≤ εR₀^{n+2}.
So h has every property required by the statement, with a δ that depends only on n and ε. ∎

Conclusion (proof of the statement; Simon 3.4, in the form used in (17)–(19) of the dependent child allard_graph, which is mentioned descriptively only).
Fix n ≥ 1 and let C_H = C_H(n) > 0 be the constant of Lemma IE. Put ω := Lⁿ(B_1) ∈ (0, ∞) (as a real number) and C := max{√2·C_H, 2, 2ωC_H²}. Then C > 0, C depends only on n, and C_H ≤ √2·C_H ≤ C.
Let ε' > 0, and let δ_h := δ > 0 be the constant of Lemma HA for ε := ε'; it depends only on n and ε'.
Let R₀ > 0 and let w be Lipschitz (constant Lw) with ∫_{B_{R₀}} ‖Dw‖² ≤ R₀ⁿ, and suppose |∫_{B_{R₀}} ∇w·∇ζ| ≤ δ_hR₀ⁿG whenever ζ is C¹ with compact support, tsupport ζ ⊆ B_{R₀}, and ‖Dζ(v)‖ ≤ G for all v.
Integrability remark. Dw is Borel and bounded by Lw, and Dζ is continuous with compact support. So both integrands of the hypotheses are bounded Borel functions on the ball B_{R₀}, which has finite measure, and their Bochner integrals are the Lebesgue integrals written here. Likewise w² and (w − a − b)² are continuous, hence integrable on bounded balls.
(1) The harmonic approximation. Lemma HA applies to (R₀, w) with δ = δ_h. It gives h harmonic on B_{R₀} such that:
- ‖Dh‖² is integrable on B_{R₀} with ∫_{B_{R₀}} ‖Dh‖² ≤ R₀ⁿ;
- (h − w)² is integrable on B_{R₀} with ∫_{B_{R₀}} (h − w)² ≤ ε'R₀^{n+2}.
(2) h² is integrable on B_{R₀}. w is continuous, so w² is bounded on the compact set closedBall(0, R₀) and integrable on B_{R₀}. Pointwise h² ≤ 2w² + 2(h − w)², and the right side is integrable on B_{R₀}. Also h² is continuous on the open ball B_{R₀}, hence a.e.-strongly measurable for Lⁿ restricted to B_{R₀}. Domination (Integrable.mono') then gives integrability.
(3) Interior estimates. By (1) and (2), Lemma IE applies with R := R₀ and this h. It gives:
- (a) |h(0)| ≤ C_H√((∫_{B_{R₀}} h²)/R₀ⁿ);
- (b) ‖Dh(0)‖ ≤ C_H;
- (c) |h(v) − h(0) − Dh(0)v| ≤ C_H‖v‖²/R₀ for ‖v‖ ≤ R₀/4.
Put a := h(0) ∈ ℝ and b := Dh(0), a continuous linear functional on ℝⁿ.
(4) Bound on b: ‖b‖ ≤ C_H ≤ C, by (b).
(5) Bound on a. Let X := (∫_{B_{R₀}} w²)/R₀ⁿ ≥ 0.
- Integrating h² ≤ 2w² + 2(h − w)² over B_{R₀} and using (1): ∫_{B_{R₀}} h² ≤ 2∫_{B_{R₀}} w² + 2ε'R₀^{n+2}. Hence (∫_{B_{R₀}} h²)/R₀ⁿ ≤ 2X + 2ε'R₀².
- Since √(x + y) ≤ √x + √y for x, y ≥ 0 and √(2ε'R₀²) = √2·√ε'·R₀: √((∫_{B_{R₀}} h²)/R₀ⁿ) ≤ √2·√X + √2·√ε'·R₀.
- By (a): |a| ≤ √2C_H·√X + √2C_H·√ε'·R₀ ≤ C·√((∫_{B_{R₀}} w²)/R₀ⁿ) + C·√ε'·R₀.
(6) Affine decay. Let θ' ∈ (0, 1/4], so B_{θ'R₀} ⊆ B_{R₀}.
- For v ∈ B_{θ'R₀} we have ‖v‖ < θ'R₀ ≤ R₀/4, so (c) gives |h(v) − a − b(v)| ≤ C_H(θ'R₀)²/R₀.
- From (x + y)² ≤ 2x² + 2y² with x := w(v) − h(v) and y := h(v) − a − b(v): (w(v) − a − b(v))² ≤ 2(h(v) − w(v))² + 2(C_H(θ'R₀)²/R₀)².
- The right side is integrable on B_{θ'R₀}, and Lⁿ(B_{θ'R₀}) = (θ'R₀)ⁿω (Measure.addHaar_ball_of_pos, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). Also ∫_{B_{θ'R₀}} (h − w)² ≤ ∫_{B_{R₀}} (h − w)² ≤ ε'R₀^{n+2}, by monotonicity of the integral of a nonnegative function in the set.
- Integrating therefore gives
 ∫_{B_{θ'R₀}} (w − a − b)² ≤ 2ε'R₀^{n+2} + 2(C_H(θ'R₀)²/R₀)²(θ'R₀)ⁿω = (2ε'/θ'^{n+2} + 2ωC_H²θ'²)(θ'R₀)^{n+2} ≤ C(ε'/θ'^{n+2} + θ'²)(θ'R₀)^{n+2},
 using 2 ≤ C and 2ωC_H² ≤ C.
(4)–(6) are the three asserted conclusions. C depends only on n, and δ_h only on n and ε'. ∎
Formalization note. The Conclusion was checked for this revision in the scratch file /tmp/dg8/lean/HarmonicConclusion.lean: theorem dg8_harmonic_affine_conclusion proves the exact frozen type of this child from Lean statements hIE and hHA of Lemmas IE and HA as stated above (neither strengthened nor weakened), with no sorry; #print axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. This confirms the constants C = max(√2·C_H, 2, 2ωC_H²), δ_h = δ(ε') and the quantifier order; it does not discharge Lemmas MV–HA themselves.
proof_key_steps: Lemma MV: a C² function with zero Laplacian satisfies the radial-kernel and ball mean value identities. The proof uses differentiation under the integral sign and integration by parts against a compactly supported radial potential.
Lemma IE: MV gives |h(0)| ≤ C_H(R^{−n}∫h²)^{1/2}, ‖Dh(0)‖ ≤ C_H, and the second-order Taylor bound |h(v) − h(0) − Dh(0)v| ≤ C_H|v|²/R on B_{R/4}.
Lemma WL (Weyl): mollifications of an L¹ function with ∫WΔζ = 0 are harmonic, and by MV they do not depend on the mollification radius. They glue to a harmonic function equal to W a.e.

Lemmas PI and RC: the Poincaré inequality on the unit ball (segment FTC and convexity), and Rellich compactness for Lipschitz functions (interior mollification, Arzelà–Ascoli, boundary-layer estimate along rays, total boundedness and completeness of L²).
Lemma EL: the C² a.e.-representative of an L² limit has Dirichlet energy at most the uniform energy bound (duality against C¹_c vector fields, exhaustion by smaller balls).
Lemma HA (Simon 3.1): by contradiction on the unit ball, using PI, RC, WL and EL; then rescale to radius R₀.
Conclusion: put a := h(0) and b := Dh(0) for the harmonic approximation h. IE and h² ≤ 2w² + 2(h − w)² give the three bounds, with C = max(√2C_H, 2, 2ω_nC_H²) and δ_h = δ(ε').

subproblems.title: Allard's regularity theorem (graph form, bounded generalized mean curvature)
subproblems.statement: Let n ≥ 1 and k ≥ 0. For every ε > 0 there are δ₀ > 0 and γ ∈ (0, 1] with the following property. Let U ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} be any set, R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep) with weight μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M (R.measure), W ⊆ U open, κ ∈ ℝ, ρ > 0, z ∈ ℝ^{n+k}, and H : ℝ^{n+k} → ℝ^{n+k} μ_R-a.e. strongly measurable with |H(x)| ≤ κ for all x, such that v(M, θ) has generalized mean curvature H in W: R.firstVariation X = ∫_M θ div_M X dHⁿ = −∫⟨X, H⟩ dμ_R for every C¹ compactly supported vector field X with tsupport X ⊆ W (div_M X(x) = trace(p_{T_xM}∘DX(x)), T_xM the approximate tangent plane of M). If the closed ball B̄_ρ(z) ⊆ W, z ∈ spt μ_R, μ_R(B̄_ρ(z)) ≤ (1 + δ₀)ω_nρⁿ and κρ ≤ δ₀, then there are linear isometries ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+k} and ι' : ℝ^k → ℝ^{n+k} with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 for all v, w, and u : ℝⁿ → ℝ^k with u(0) = 0, u of class C¹ on the open ball B_{γρ}(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ with ‖Du(v)‖ ≤ ε there, such that spt μ_R ∩ B_{γρ}(z) = {z + ιv + ι'u(v) : |v| < γρ} ∩ B_{γρ}(z) (open balls). This is Allard's Regularity Theorem (Simon Ch. 5, 5.2 with Remark 5.3) for integer multiplicity varifolds with bounded generalized mean curvature, i.e. the case p = 2n of hypotheses 5.1. (The frozen Lean type is character-identical to that of DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.epsilon_regularity-a1.allard_graph-a1, not yet comparator-accepted; it is declared here under the fresh name Submission.dimred_cdg_allard_bounded_curvature_graph.)

subproblems.natural_proof:
Provenance and prerequisites. This is the independently reviewed proof supplied for the identical frozen type at DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.epsilon_regularity-a1.allard_graph-a1 (status speculative-ready, not comparator-accepted, so it is declared here under a fresh name). Two changes close it over this decomposition, and Part 8.5 states the a.e. tangent-plane identity on the ball A⁺ ⊇ A that contains every point used in 8.7:
(1) Measurability. The measurability of the approximate-tangent projection x ↦ p_x, used in Parts 1, 3–5, 7 and 8, is taken from the sibling tangent_projection_aesm and transferred to μ in paragraph (M0) below.
(2) Harmonic approximation. Part 6 (Simon 3.1–3.4), which the earlier text derived from the Poincaré inequality, Rellich's compactness theorem, Weyl's lemma and the mean value estimates, is replaced by the sibling harmonic_affine. The supplied proof of that sibling proves all of these inputs. Steps 7–8 of Part 7 are rewritten to use its conclusion.
Siblings used: tangent_projection_aesm (Submission.imrep_approxTangent_starProjection_aesm, comparator-accepted) and harmonic_affine (Submission.dimred_cdg_harmonic_affine_approximation). Every other input is a theorem of the pinned Mathlib or SimonGMT, cited by name. This child is used in step 5 of the sibling origin_regularity, with H ≡ 0 and κ = 0.
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 5 §§2–5, the proof of the Allard Regularity Theorem 5.2 (chapter-05.txt lines 1008–1032 for 5.1–5.2; Lemma 2.1, Remark 2.2, (2.3)–(2.4), Affine Approximation 2.5, Lipschitz Approximation 2.6, Corollary 2.7, Harmonic Approximation 3.1–3.4, Tilt-excess Decay 4.5–4.6 and the proof of 5.2, printed pp. 106–124), with the monotonicity identity of Ch. 4, 3.3–3.17 (chapter-04.txt lines 215–455). The printed proof is copied with p := 2n and bounded mean curvature: since |H| ≤ κ, each term ρ^{1−n/p}(∫_{B_ρ}|H|^p dμ)^{1/p} of Simon is at most C(n)κρ, so Simon's smallness hypothesis on H is replaced by κρ ≤ δ, Simon's E_* by E_*(ξ, r, S) := max{E(ξ, r, S), δ^{−1}κ²r²}, Simon's decay exponent 2(1 − n/p) equals 1, and the bounded-H monotonicity 3.17 replaces 4.7. Departures from the printed text are marked Correction.

Notation. E := ℝ^{n+k}; B_t(x) is the closed ball, B̆_t(x) the open ball (Lean ball); Bⁿ, B̆ⁿ denote balls in ℝⁿ or in an n-plane; ω_n := unitBallVolume n. M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult (a positive integer on M), μ := R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M with Hⁿ := μHE[n]. Since W ⊆ U is open and IMRep.locallyIntegrable_mult holds on compact subsets of U, μ and Hⁿ⌞M are finite on compact subsets of W. For Hⁿ-a.e. (hence μ-a.e.) x ∈ M the approximate tangent plane T_xM := approxTangentPlane n M x exists and is n-dimensional (IMRep.orients); p_x is the orthogonal projection onto T_xM and p_x^⊥ := I − p_x. For an n-plane S, p_S and p_S^⊥ := I − p_S. |A| is the Hilbert–Schmidt norm and ‖A‖ ≤ |A| the operator norm. div_M X(x) := trace(p_x∘DX(x)), so R.firstVariation X = ∫ div_M X dμ. The hypothesis is (MC): ∫ div_M X dμ = −∫ X·H dμ for every C¹ compactly supported X : E → E with tsupport X ⊆ W; and |H| ≤ κ everywhere (so κ ≥ 0). Tilt-excess (Simon 4.1): E(ξ, r, S) := r^{−n}∫_{B_r(ξ)}|p_x − p_S|² dμ(x). α := 1/(2n+2). No translation, dilation or rotation of R is used: balls have arbitrary centres and rotations are only choices of orthonormal coordinates. For readability we write z = 0 (read B_t(y) as B_t(z + y)).

(M0) Measurability of the tangent-plane field (sibling tangent_projection_aesm).
- The sibling tangent_projection_aesm (Submission.imrep_approxTangent_starProjection_aesm), applied with P := n + k and our U and R, says that x ↦ p_x = (approxTangentPlane n M x).starProjection is AEStronglyMeasurable for Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M.
- Transfer to μ. μ = R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ is absolutely continuous with respect to Hⁿ⌞M (MeasureTheory.withDensity_absolutelyContinuous). Hence x ↦ p_x is AEStronglyMeasurable for μ (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac), and also for every measure ν ≪ μ. Examples are μ⌞A for any set A and, in 8.5–8.7, Hⁿ⌞(F ∩ B_{σ₀/8}(0)) ≤ μ.
- Consequences.
 (i) For a C¹ field X, div_M X(x) = trace(p_x∘DX(x)) is a continuous function of (p_x, DX(x)), with DX continuous. So it is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, and |div_M X| ≤ (n + k)·sup‖DX‖. Likewise |p_x − p_S|², |p_x^⊥(x − y)|², (p_xe)·∇ζ(x) and p_x(∇fʲ(v), 0)·∇ζ̃₀(x) are μ-a.e. strongly measurable and bounded on bounded sets, since ‖p_x‖ ≤ 1 and |p_x|² = trace p_x ≤ n + k. As μ is finite on compact subsets of W, all of them are μ-integrable on compact subsets of W.
 (ii) θ is a measurable ℕ-valued density, so R.firstVariation X = ∫_M θ·div_M X dHⁿ = ∫ div_M X dμ (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul). This identity is used to write (MC).
 (iii) (i) justifies the following steps: the differentiation under the integral sign and the Fubini–Tonelli exchanges in 1.1; Chebyshev's inequality in Part 4(iv); the integrals in Parts 3, 5 and 7; and Lebesgue's differentiation theorem for x ↦ p_x in 8.5. There it is applied to the finite measure ν := μ⌞B_{σ₀/4}(0). ν is finite because the closed ball B_{σ₀/4}(0) is a compact subset of W, and p is ν-integrable, being bounded and ν-a.e. strongly measurable. ν agrees with μ on subsets of B̆_{σ₀/4}(0), which contains every ball used in 8.5–8.7.

Part 0. Constants.
0.1 Fix c₀ = c₀(n, k) ∈ (0, 1/4] as in 8.6 and put L₀ := min{ε, c₀}.
0.2 Parts 2–8 introduce finitely many smallness thresholds for δ, each depending only on n, k and L₀; δ_A ∈ (0, 1/8] denotes their minimum. We prove (★): if δ := δ_A and (SA) below holds for some ρ > 0, then there are an n-plane T₀ and a map f : T₀ → T₀^⊥, C¹ on A := {v ∈ T₀ : |v| < δρ/16} with ‖Df‖ ≤ L₀ there and f(0) = 0, such that spt μ ∩ B̆_{δρ/16}(0) = {v + f(v) : v ∈ A} ∩ B̆_{δρ/16}(0). Part 9 derives the Lean statement with δ₀ := δ_A and γ := δ_A/16.

Part 1. Monotonicity and densities (Simon Ch. 4, 3.3–3.17, 4.10; Ch. 3, 1.5).
1.1 Let y ∈ E, R > 0 with B_R(y) ⊆ W, r := |x − y|, D^⊥r(x) := p_x^⊥((x − y)/r). Then for 0 < s < t < R:
 (M1) ∫_{B_t(y)∖B_s(y)} r^{−n}|D^⊥r|² dμ ≤ e^{κt}t^{−n}μ(B_t(y)) − e^{κs}s^{−n}μ(B_s(y));
 (M2) e^{−κt}t^{−n}μ(B_t(y)) − e^{−κs}s^{−n}μ(B_s(y)) ≤ ∫_{B_t(y)∖B_s(y)} r^{−n}|D^⊥r|² dμ.
 Here r^{−n}|D^⊥r|² = |x − y|^{−n−2}|p_x^⊥(x − y)|².
 Proof (Simon 3.2–3.6, 3.16–3.17). Let ε₁ ∈ (0, 1) with (1+ε₁)t < R and φ ∈ C¹(ℝ) with 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1, φ' ≤ 0, φ ≡ 1 on (−∞, 1], φ ≡ 0 on [1+ε₁, ∞). For τ ∈ (0, t] let X_τ(x) := φ(r/τ)(x − y); it is C¹ (it equals x − y near y) with tsupport in B_{(1+ε₁)τ}(y) ⊆ W. At μ-a.e. x, DX_τ = φ(r/τ)I + τ^{−1}φ'(r/τ)(x − y)⊗∇r, so div_M X_τ = nφ(r/τ) + (r/τ)φ'(r/τ)(1 − |D^⊥r|²), because trace p_x = n and p_x∇r·∇r = 1 − |D^⊥r|². With I(τ) := ∫φ(r/τ)dμ and J(τ) := ∫φ(r/τ)|D^⊥r|²dμ (C¹ in τ by differentiation under the integral) and (r/τ)φ'(r/τ) = −τ∂_τ[φ(r/τ)], (MC) gives nI(τ) − τI'(τ) + τJ'(τ) = −ϑ(τ), where ϑ(τ) := ∫φ(r/τ)(x − y)·H dμ and |ϑ(τ)| ≤ (1+ε₁)κτI(τ). Thus g(τ) := τ^{−n}I(τ) satisfies g' = τ^{−n}J' + e with |e| ≤ cg, c := (1+ε₁)κ; as J' ≥ 0, (e^{cτ}g)' ≥ τ^{−n}J' and (e^{−cτ}g)' ≤ τ^{−n}J'. Integrating over [s, t]: ∫_s^t τ^{−n}J' dτ ≤ e^{ct}g(t) − e^{cs}g(s) and e^{−ct}g(t) − e^{−cs}g(s) ≤ ∫_s^t τ^{−n}J' dτ. By Fubini (Simon 3.5), ∫_s^t τ^{−n}J'(τ)dτ = ∫|D^⊥r|²(∫_s^t τ^{−n}∂_τφ(r/τ)dτ)dμ, and the inner integral lies between r^{−n}(φ(r/t) − φ(r/s)) and (1+ε₁)ⁿr^{−n}(φ(r/t) − φ(r/s)); moreover 1_{B_t∖B_{(1+ε₁)s}} ≤ φ(r/t) − φ(r/s) ≤ 1_{B_{(1+ε₁)t}∖B_s} and μ(B_τ(y)) ≤ I(τ) ≤ μ(B_{(1+ε₁)τ}(y)). Letting ε₁ ↓ 0 (closed balls decrease to closed balls) gives (M1) and (M2).
1.2 Consequences. (a) τ ↦ e^{κτ}τ^{−n}μ(B_τ(y)) is nondecreasing on (0, R) (cf. library HasGeneralizedMeanCurvatureIn.exp_normalizedBallMass_monotoneOn). (b) Θ(μ, y) := lim_{τ↓0} μ(B_τ(y))/(ω_nτⁿ) exists in [0, ∞) for every y ∈ W. (c) For 0 < t < R: ∫_{B_t(y)} |x − y|^{−n−2}|p_x^⊥(x − y)|² dμ ≤ e^{κt}t^{−n}μ(B_t(y)) − ω_nΘ(μ, y) (let s ↓ 0 in (M1); μ({y}) = 0 as n ≥ 1). (d) If μ(B_s(y)) = 0 then μ(B_t(y)) ≤ e^{κt}tⁿ∫_{B_t(y)∖B_s(y)} |x − y|^{−n−2}|p_x^⊥(x − y)|² dμ (by (M2)).
1.3 Θ(μ, y) ≥ 1 for y ∈ spt μ ∩ W (Simon Ch. 4, 4.10(1)). (i) If x ∈ M and T_xM exists, then Hⁿ(M ∩ B_τ(x))/(ω_nτⁿ) → 1 (Simon Ch. 3, 1.5(3): test the definition of the approximate tangent plane with continuous compactly supported functions squeezed between the indicators of B_{1−ε''}(0) and B_{1+ε''}(0)); as μ ≥ Hⁿ⌞M, Θ(μ, x) ≥ 1. So Θ(μ, ·) ≥ 1 μ-a.e. in W. (ii) Θ(μ, ·) is upper semicontinuous on W: if y_j → y ∈ W and B_{τ+ε''}(y) ⊆ W, then B_τ(y_j) ⊆ B_{τ+ε''}(y) for large j and 1.2(a) gives Θ(μ, y_j) ≤ ω_n^{−1}e^{κτ}τ^{−n}μ(B_{τ+ε''}(y)); let j → ∞, then ε'' ↓ 0, then τ ↓ 0. (iii) If y ∈ spt μ ∩ W, every B̆_{1/j}(y) has positive μ-measure, hence contains x_j with Θ(μ, x_j) ≥ 1; by (ii), Θ(μ, y) ≥ 1.
1.4 Hⁿ((spt μ ∩ W) ∖ M) = 0. Let A' := (spt μ ∩ W) ∖ M, so μ(A') = 0. Given ε'' > 0 choose an open O with A' ⊆ O ⊆ W and μ(O) < ε'' (outer regularity of the Radon measure μ⌞W). For x ∈ A' the upper n-density of μ⌞O at x equals Θ(μ, x) ≥ 1, so the comparison theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.3; library simon_theorem_3_3) gives Hⁿ(A') ≤ μ(O) < ε''.
1.5 θ(x) ≤ Θ(μ, x) for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ W. For an integer m ≥ 1 let M_m := {x ∈ M : θ(x) = m}. By the Upper Density Theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6 and Remark 3.7(2) for the locally finite measure Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ W); library simon_theorem_3_6), the upper density of Hⁿ⌞(M ∖ M_m) vanishes at Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_m ∩ W; with 1.3(i), Hⁿ(M_m ∩ B_τ(x))/(ω_nτⁿ) → 1 there, and μ ≥ m·Hⁿ⌞M_m gives Θ(μ, x) ≥ m = θ(x).
1.6 Tangent planes on a Lipschitz graph (Simon Ch. 3, 1.5(2) and the proof of 1.6). Let S be an n-plane, a ∈ E, f : S → S^⊥ Lipschitz, Φ_f(v) := a + v + f(v), F := Φ_f(S). Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ F ∩ W, writing x = Φ_f(v): f is differentiable at v and T_xM = graph Df(v) := {w + Df(v)w : w ∈ S}.
 Proof. (i) By Rademacher's theorem (Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt) and Lebesgue's differentiation theorem, Lⁿ-a.e. v ∈ S is a differentiability point of f and a Lebesgue point of Df; the exceptional set N satisfies Hⁿ(Φ_f(N)) = 0 because Φ_f is Lipschitz. (ii) For v ∉ N, F has approximate tangent plane graph Df(v) at x = Φ_f(v): for ψ₀ ∈ C_c(E) with spt ψ₀ ⊆ B_{R'}(0), the area formula gives ∫_{η_{x,λ}(F)} ψ₀ dHⁿ = ∫_S ψ₀(w + f_λ(w)) J_f(v + λw) dw, where f_λ(w) := (f(v + λw) − f(v))/λ and J_f is the area Jacobian of Φ_f; the integrand vanishes for |w| > R' and is uniformly bounded; f_λ → Df(v) locally uniformly and J_f(v + λ·) → J_f(v) in L¹_loc (Lebesgue point of Df; the Jacobian is a locally Lipschitz function of Df), so the integral tends to ∫_S ψ₀(w + Df(v)w) J_f(v) dw = ∫_{graph Df(v)} ψ₀ dHⁿ. (iii) By the Upper Density Theorem, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ F ∩ W the upper densities of Hⁿ⌞(F ∖ M) and of Hⁿ⌞(M ∖ F) at x vanish (both sets have locally finite Hⁿ-measure in W). (iv) At such x with v ∉ N, |∫_{η_{x,λ}(M)} ψ₀ dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{x,λ}(F)} ψ₀ dHⁿ| ≤ sup|ψ₀|·λ^{−n}Hⁿ(((M ∖ F) ∪ (F ∖ M)) ∩ B_{λR'}(x)) → 0, so M has approximate tangent plane graph Df(v) at x, and by uniqueness (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique) T_xM = graph Df(v).

Part 2. Standing assumption and density bounds (Simon 2.3–2.4).
(SA) δ ∈ (0, 1/8], ρ > 0, 0 ∈ spt μ, B_ρ(0) ⊆ W, μ(B_ρ(0)) ≤ (1 + δ)ω_nρⁿ and κρ ≤ δ. Put r₁ := δρ. As B_ρ(0) is compact and W open, fix ρ⁺ ∈ (ρ, 2ρ) with B_{ρ⁺}(0) ⊆ W. For y ∈ B_{4r₁}(0) we have B_{ρ⁺−4r₁}(y) ⊆ W and ρ⁺ − 4r₁ > (1 − 4δ)ρ ≥ ρ/2 ≥ 4r₁; so 1.1–1.2 apply at y for all radii ≤ (1 − 4δ)ρ.
2.1 For every y ∈ B_{4r₁}(0) and 0 < t ≤ (1 − 4δ)ρ: μ(B_t(y)) ≤ (1 + c(δ))ω_ntⁿ with c(δ) := e^{δ}(1 − 4δ)^{−n}(1 + δ) − 1 ≤ C₁δ. Indeed by 1.2(a) with t' := (1 − 4δ)ρ and B_{t'}(y) ⊆ B_ρ(0): t^{−n}μ(B_t(y)) ≤ e^{κt'}t'^{−n}μ(B_ρ(0)) ≤ e^{δ}(1 − 4δ)^{−n}(1 + δ)ω_n.
2.2 For every y ∈ spt μ ∩ B_{4r₁}(0) and 0 < t ≤ (1 − 4δ)ρ: μ(B_t(y)) ≥ e^{−δ}ω_ntⁿ, by 1.2(a) and 1.3: e^{κt}t^{−n}μ(B_t(y)) ≥ ω_nΘ(μ, y) ≥ ω_n. At x ∈ spt μ: if x ∈ B_σ(ξ) and |x'| < r/2, then x ∈ B̆_{3r/4}(ξ) (Step 3) and ζ = ζ̃₀ near x; if x ∈ B_σ(ξ) and |x'| ≥ r/2, then ζ̃₀ and ζ vanish near x (spt ζ₀ is a compact subset of B̆ⁿ_{r/2}(0)); if x ∉ B_σ(ξ), ζ vanishes near x. Hence (8') holds with ∇ζ replaced by ∇ζ̃₀ = (∇ζ₀(x'), 0) and sup|∇ζ| by sup|∇ζ₀|. At μ-a.e. x ∈ M₁, with a := (∇fʲ(x'), 0) and b := ∇ζ̃₀(x) in T: ∇^Mf̃ʲ·∇ζ̃₀ = (p_xa)·b = a·b − (p_Tp_x^⊥p_Ta)·b and p_Tp_x^⊥p_T = (p_T − p_x)p_x^⊥(p_T − p_x), so (11): |∇^Mf̃ʲ·∇ζ̃₀ − ∇fʲ(x')·∇ζ₀(x')| ≤ |p_x − p_T|²|∇fʲ(x')||∇ζ₀(x')|. With |∇fʲ| ≤ 1 and (4'):
 (12') |r^{−n}∫_{M₁∩B_r(ξ)} ∇fʲ(x')·∇ζ₀(x') dμ| ≤ C sup|∇ζ₀|(δ^{1/2}E₀^{1/2} + E₀),
 and applying (11) with b := a and (9'):
 (13') r^{−n}∫_{M₁∩B_r(ξ)} |∇fʲ(x')|² dμ ≤ CE₀.
Step 6 (transfer to ℝⁿ; Simon (14)–(16)). Let J_f(v) := (det(I + Df(v)ᵀDf(v)))^{1/2} ∈ [1, 2^{n/2}], so |J_f − 1| ≤ C|Df|², and θ_F(v) := θ(Φ_f(v)) if Φ_f(v) ∈ M, θ_F(v) := 0 otherwise. By the area formula for the injective Lipschitz map Φ_f (Simon Ch. 2, 3.5) and Step 3, for every Borel g on ℝⁿ supported in B̆ⁿ_{r/2}(0) and nonnegative or integrable: ∫_{M₁∩B_r(ξ)} g(x') dμ = ∫_{Bⁿ_{r/2}(0)} g(v)θ_F(v)J_f(v) dv. Let Z₀ := {v ∈ B̆ⁿ_{r/2}(0) : Φ_f(v) ∉ M} and Z₂ := {v ∈ B̆ⁿ_{r/2}(0) : θ_F(v) ≥ 2}. By 1.4, (4') and J_f ≥ 1: Lⁿ(Z₀) ≤ Hⁿ((F ∖ spt μ) ∩ B_r(ξ)) + Hⁿ((spt μ ∩ W) ∖ M) ≤ C₇σⁿE₀ ≤ CrⁿE₀; by 2.4, Lⁿ(Z₂) = 0. Off Z₀ ∪ Z₂ we have θ_F = 1. Hence from (12'), (13'):
 (16') r^{−n}∫_{Bⁿ_{r/2}(0)} |∇fʲ|² dv ≤ CE₀,
 (15') |r^{−n}∫_{Bⁿ_{r/2}(0)} ∇fʲ·∇ζ₀ dv| ≤ C sup|∇ζ₀|(δ^{1/2}E₀^{1/2} + E₀) ≤ C₁₂δ^αE₀^{1/2} sup|∇ζ₀|,
 using ∫_{Z₀}|∇fʲ||∇ζ₀| ≤ sup|∇ζ₀|Lⁿ(Z₀), |θ_FJ_f − 1| ≤ C|Df|² off Z₀ ∪ Z₂ together with (16'), and E₀ ≤ (C₃δ^{2α})^{1/2}E₀^{1/2}, δ^{1/2} ≤ δ^α. Correction: Simon's (15) has the factor δ^{1/2}E₀^{1/2}; since only E₀ ≤ Cδ^{1/(n+1)} is available, the factor is δ^{1/(2n+2)}E₀^{1/2}, which suffices.
Step 7 (harmonic approximation; Simon (17)). Recall R₀ = r/2 = σ/8 and E₀ > 0.
- By (16'), ∫_{Bⁿ_{R₀}(0)} |∇fʲ|² ≤ Crⁿ E₀ = 2ⁿC E₀R₀ⁿ ≤ C₁₃E₀R₀ⁿ for j = 1, …, k, with C₁₃ := max{2ⁿC, 1}.
- Put wʲ := (C₁₃E₀)^{−1/2}fʲ. It is Lipschitz on ℝⁿ, since f is, and ∫_{B̆ⁿ_{R₀}(0)} |∇wʲ|² ≤ R₀ⁿ.
- Let ζ be C¹ with compact support, tsupport ζ ⊆ B̆ⁿ_{R₀}(0) = B̆ⁿ_{r/2}(0), and |∇ζ| ≤ G. Then ζ is admissible as ζ₀ in Step 5, and sup|∇ζ| ≤ G. So (15') gives
 |∫_{B̆ⁿ_{R₀}(0)} ∇wʲ·∇ζ| ≤ (C₁₃E₀)^{−1/2}·C₁₂δ^αE₀^{1/2}·rⁿ·G = C₁₄δ^αR₀ⁿG, with C₁₄ := 2ⁿC₁₂C₁₃^{−1/2}.
- Hence, provided C₁₄δ^α ≤ δ_h(n, ε'), 6.1 applies to each wʲ. It gives aʲ ∈ ℝ and linear bʲ : ℝⁿ → ℝ satisfying (6a)–(6c).
- Define the affine map λ : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ by λʲ(v) := (C₁₃E₀)^{1/2}(aʲ + bʲ(v)). Write λ(v) = λ(0) + Av, with A : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ linear and Aʲ = (C₁₃E₀)^{1/2}bʲ.
Correction: Simon's harmonic u and its affine part λ(v) = u(0) + Du(0)v are replaced by the affine map returned directly by the sibling.
Step 8 (affine approximation; Simon (18)–(19)).
- Slope. By (6a), |A| ≤ (Σ_j|Aʲ|²)^{1/2} ≤ √k·C₁₃^{1/2}C_HA·E₀^{1/2}. Since E₀ ≤ C₃δ^{2α}, this gives |A| ≤ CE₀^{1/2} ≤ Cδ^α.
- Constant term. We use (6b), sup|f| ≤ C₇δ^ασ = 8C₇δ^αR₀ (Part 5A), Lⁿ(B̆ⁿ_{R₀}(0)) = ω_nR₀ⁿ, E₀^{1/2} ≤ C₃^{1/2}δ^α and ε' ≤ 1 (Step 10). They give
 (18') |λ(0)| ≤ Σ_j (C₁₃E₀)^{1/2}|aʲ| ≤ Σ_j [C_HA(R₀^{−n}∫_{B̆ⁿ_{R₀}(0)} (fʲ)²)^{1/2} + C_HA(C₁₃E₀)^{1/2}√ε'R₀] ≤ kC_HAω_n^{1/2}·8C₇δ^αR₀ + kC_HAC₁₃^{1/2}C₃^{1/2}δ^αR₀ =: C₁₅R₀δ^α.
- L² approximation. By (6c), for θ' ∈ (0, 1/4]: ∫_{B̆ⁿ_{θ'R₀}(0)} |f − λ|² = Σ_j C₁₃E₀∫_{B̆ⁿ_{θ'R₀}(0)} (wʲ − aʲ − bʲ)² ≤ kC₁₃C_HA(ε'θ'^{−n−2} + θ'²)(θ'R₀)^{n+2}E₀. Hence
 (19') (θ'R₀)^{−n−2}∫_{Bⁿ_{θ'R₀}(0)} |f − λ|² dv ≤ C(θ'^{−n−2}ε' + θ'²)E₀,
 for the open and, equivalently, the closed ball (the sphere is Lⁿ-null).
Step 9 (the new plane; Simon (20)–(22)). Let S := {(w, Aw) : w ∈ ℝⁿ}, an n-plane, and τ := ξ + (0, λ(0)). Require C₁₅δ^α ≤ θ'/4; then |τ − ξ| ≤ θ'R₀/4 and B_{θ'R₀}(τ) ⊆ B_{σ/2}(ξ). For x = Φ_f(v) with |v| ≤ θ'R₀, dist(x − τ, S) ≤ |f(v) − λ(v)|, and F ∩ B_{θ'R₀}(τ) ⊆ Φ_f(Bⁿ_{θ'R₀}(0)). Split ∫_{B_{θ'R₀}(τ)} dist(x − τ, S)² dμ into the parts on F and off F. On F, μ⌞F ≤ Hⁿ⌞F (θ = 1 μ-a.e. there by 2.4) and the area formula with J_f ≤ 2^{n/2} bound it by 2^{n/2}∫_{Bⁿ_{θ'R₀}(0)} |f − λ|². Off F, each x ∈ spt μ ∩ B_{θ'R₀}(τ) has dist(x − τ, S) ≤ |x''| + |λ(0)| + |A||x'| ≤ Cδ^ασ by (2'), (18'), |A| ≤ Cδ^α (Step 8) and |x'| ≤ σ, and μ(B_{θ'R₀}(τ) ∖ F) ≤ C₇σⁿE₀ by (4'). With σ = 8R₀ this gives
 (θ'R₀)^{−n−2}∫_{B_{θ'R₀}(τ)} dist(x − τ, S)² dμ ≤ C(θ'^{−n−2}ε' + θ'^{−n−2}δ^{2α} + θ'²)E₀.
 Correction: Simon's middle term Cδ^{1/(n+1)}E₀ omits the factor θ'^{−n−2}; this is harmless because θ' is fixed before δ. Now 3.1 at (τ, θ'R₀) (B_{θ'R₀}(τ) ⊆ W, μ(B_{θ'R₀}(τ)) ≤ 2ω_n(θ'R₀)ⁿ by 2.1, κ²(θ'R₀)² ≤ κ²σ² ≤ δE₀) gives
 (20') E(τ, θ'R₀/2, S) ≤ C(θ'^{−n−2}(ε' + δ^{2α}) + θ'² + δ)E₀,
 and since B_{θ'R₀/4}(ξ) ⊆ B_{θ'R₀/2}(τ) (21'),
 (22') E(ξ, θ'R₀/4, S) ≤ 2ⁿE(τ, θ'R₀/2, S) ≤ C₁₆(θ'^{−n−2}(ε' + δ^{2α}) + θ'² + δ)E₀.
Step 10 (choice of constants; Simon (23)). Put θ₀ := θ'R₀/(4σ) = θ'/32. Choose θ' ∈ (0, ¼] with C₁₆θ'² ≤ θ'/128, then ε' ∈ (0, 1] with C₁₆θ'^{−n−2}ε' ≤ θ'/128, then δ₂ ∈ (0, δ₁] so small that for δ ≤ δ₂: δ^α ≤ β (Step 2), C₁₁δ^α ≤ 1/16 and C₇δ^α ≤ 1/16 (Step 3), C₁₄δ^α ≤ δ_h(n, ε') (Step 7), C₁₅δ^α ≤ θ'/4 (Step 9), C₁₆θ'^{−n−2}δ^{2α} ≤ θ'/128 and C₁₆δ ≤ θ'/128. Then E(ξ, θ₀σ, S) ≤ (θ'/32)E₀ = θ₀E₀ and δ^{−1}κ²(θ₀σ)² = θ₀²δ^{−1}κ²σ² ≤ θ₀E₀, so E_*(ξ, θ₀σ, S) ≤ θ₀E_*(ξ, σ, T).

Part 8. Iteration and the graph (proof of Simon 5.2).
Assume (SA) with δ ≤ δ₂ and the smallness conditions of 8.4. Put σ₀ := r₁ = δρ.
8.1 Base plane. Part 4 at (0, 2σ₀) gives T₀ with E(0, σ₀, T₀) ≤ C₃δ^{2α} and dist(x, T₀) ≤ 2C₃δ^ασ₀ for x ∈ spt μ ∩ B_{2σ₀}(0). For ξ ∈ spt μ ∩ B_{σ₀/2}(0), B_{σ₀/2}(ξ) ⊆ B_{σ₀}(0), so E_*(ξ, σ₀/2, T₀) ≤ max{2ⁿC₃δ^{2α}, δ³} ≤ E₀ := 2ⁿC₃δ^{2α} (C₃ ≥ 1).
8.2 Iteration. Fix ξ ∈ spt μ ∩ B_{σ₀/2}(0) and put σ_j := θ₀^jσ₀/2 ∈ (0, r₁]. Applying 7A inductively at (ξ, σ_j, S_j) gives n-planes S₀ := T₀, S₁, S₂, … with E_*(ξ, σ_{j+1}, S_{j+1}) ≤ θ₀E_*(ξ, σ_j, S_j), so E_*(ξ, σ_j, S_j) ≤ θ₀^jE₀, and by 7B |p_{S_{j+1}} − p_{S_j}| ≤ (C₁₀θ₀^{−n}θ₀^jE₀)^{1/2}. Summing the geometric series, p_{S_j} converges to an orthogonal projection of rank n (the set of such projections is closed); its range is called S(ξ). Then |p_{S(ξ)} − p_{S_j}| ≤ Cθ₀^{j/2}E₀^{1/2} and |p_{S(ξ)} − p_{T₀}| ≤ CE₀^{1/2}. Correction: Simon's (2) writes η^jσ₀ for η^jσ₀/2.
8.3 Decay at all scales (Simon (7)–(8)). For 0 < s ≤ σ₀/2 choose j with σ_{j+1} < s ≤ σ_j. Then E(ξ, s, S(ξ)) ≤ 2(σ_j/s)ⁿE(ξ, σ_j, S_j) + 2s^{−n}μ(B_s(ξ))|p_{S_j} − p_{S(ξ)}|² ≤ Cθ₀^jE₀ ≤ C(s/σ₀)E₀ (as θ₀^j = 2σ_j/σ₀ < 2s/(θ₀σ₀)). Thus for ξ ∈ spt μ ∩ B_{σ₀/2}(0) and 0 < s ≤ σ₀/2:
 (7'') E(ξ, s, S(ξ)) ≤ C₁₇(s/σ₀)E₀, and (8'') E(ξ, s, T₀) ≤ 2E(ξ, s, S(ξ)) + 4ω_n|p_{S(ξ)} − p_{T₀}|² ≤ C₁₈E₀.
8.4 The graph (Simon (9)). Apply 5B at (0, σ₀, T₀, L := L₀, C₆ := 2C₃): (i) and (ii) hold by 8.1; the extra hypothesis holds by (8'') provided C₁₈2ⁿC₃δ^{2α} ≤ β'²L₀²; and 5A needs δ^α ≤ βL₀. Also require C₇δ^α ≤ 1/32. These are the smallness conditions of this part (they depend on L₀). We obtain a Lipschitz f : T₀ → T₀^⊥ with Lip f ≤ L₀, sup|f| ≤ C₇δ^ασ₀ ≤ σ₀/32 and
 (9'') spt μ ∩ B_{σ₀/8}(0) = F ∩ B_{σ₀/8}(0), F := graph_0 f = {v + f(v) : v ∈ T₀}.
 Since 0 ∈ spt μ, 0 = Φ_f(v) for some v, so v = 0 and f(0) = 0.
8.5 Tangent planes (Simon (10)). Let A := {v ∈ T₀ : |v| < σ₀/16} and A⁺ := {v ∈ T₀ : |v| < 3σ₀/32} ⊇ A. For v ∈ A⁺, |Φ_f(v)| ≤ |v| + |f(v)| < 3σ₀/32 + σ₀/32 = σ₀/8 (sup|f| ≤ σ₀/32 by 8.4), so Φ_f(v) ∈ spt μ ∩ B_{σ₀/8}(0) by (9''). By (9''), 1.4 and θ ≥ 1, Hⁿ⌞(F ∩ B_{σ₀/8}(0)) ≤ μ; hence, using J_f ≥ 1 and the area formula, every μ-null set Z has Lⁿ-null Φ_f-preimage in A⁺: Lⁿ(A⁺ ∩ Φ_f^{−1}(Z)) ≤ Hⁿ(Φ_f(A⁺) ∩ Z) ≤ μ(Z) = 0. So by 1.6, 1.4 and Lebesgue's differentiation theorem for the finite Radon measure ν := μ⌞B_{σ₀/4}(0) of (M0)(iii) (Mathlib VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub for the Besicovitch Vitali family of ν; ν = μ on subsets of B̆_{σ₀/4}(0)), for Lⁿ-a.e. v ∈ A⁺ the point ξ_v := Φ_f(v) satisfies: f is differentiable at v, ξ_v ∈ M, T_{ξ_v}M = graph Df(v), and ξ_v is a μ-Lebesgue point of x ↦ p_x; call such v good. At a good v, ξ_v ∈ spt μ ∩ B_{σ₀/8}(0) ⊆ spt μ ∩ B_{σ₀/2}(0), so (7'') applies at ξ_v and gives p_{S(ξ_v)} = p_{graph Df(v)}: indeed |p_{ξ_v} − p_{S(ξ_v)}|²·s^{−n}μ(B_s(ξ_v)) ≤ 2s^{−n}∫_{B_s(ξ_v)} |p_x − p_{ξ_v}|² dμ + 2E(ξ_v, s, S(ξ_v)) → 0 as s ↓ 0, while s^{−n}μ(B_s(ξ_v)) ≥ ω_n/2. (The larger ball A⁺ is needed in 8.7, where the identity p_{Φ_f(v')} = p_{graph Df(v')} is used at points v' with |v'| < σ₀/16 + σ₀/64, which may lie outside A.)
8.6 Projections of graphs. For linear A₁, A₂ : T₀ → T₀^⊥ with ‖A₁‖, ‖A₂‖ ≤ c₀: the T₀^⊥←T₀ block of p_{graph A} is A(I + AᵀA)^{−1}, so the corresponding block of p_{graph A₁} − p_{graph A₂} equals (A₁ − A₂)(I + A₁ᵀA₁)^{−1} + A₂(I + A₁ᵀA₁)^{−1}(A₂ᵀA₂ − A₁ᵀA₁)(I + A₂ᵀA₂)^{−1}, whose Hilbert–Schmidt norm is at least (1 + c₀²)^{−1}|A₁ − A₂| − 2c₀²√(n+k)|A₁ − A₂| ≥ ½|A₁ − A₂| when c₀ = c₀(n, k) is small (this fixes c₀ in 0.1). Hence |A₁ − A₂| ≤ 2|p_{graph A₁} − p_{graph A₂}|.
8.7 Campanato estimate (Simon (11)). Let v ∈ A be good (8.5) and 0 < s ≤ σ₀/64. For v' ∈ Bⁿ_s(v): |v'| ≤ |v| + s < σ₀/16 + σ₀/64 < 3σ₀/32, so v' ∈ A⁺; |Φ_f(v') − ξ_v| ≤ √2|v' − v| < 2s (Lip f ≤ 1); and B_{2s}(ξ_v) ⊆ B_{σ₀/8}(0), since |ξ_v| < σ₀/16 + σ₀/32 = 3σ₀/32 and 2s ≤ σ₀/32. Since Lⁿ-a.e. point of A⁺ is good, p_{Φ_f(v')} = p_{graph Df(v')} for Lⁿ-a.e. v' ∈ Bⁿ_s(v) (8.5). By 8.6 (Lip f ≤ L₀ ≤ c₀), the area formula (J_f ≥ 1), Hⁿ⌞(F ∩ B_{σ₀/8}(0)) ≤ μ and (7'') with 2s ≤ σ₀/2:
 ∫_{Bⁿ_s(v)} |Df(v') − Df(v)|² dv' ≤ 4∫_{F∩B_{2s}(ξ_v)} |p_x − p_{S(ξ_v)}|² dHⁿ ≤ 4∫_{B_{2s}(ξ_v)} |p_x − p_{S(ξ_v)}|² dμ ≤ 4(2s)ⁿC₁₇(2s/σ₀)E₀.
 For good v₁, v₂ ∈ A (a set of full measure in A) with s := |v₁ − v₂| ≤ σ₀/64, averaging |Df(v₁) − Df(v₂)|² ≤ 2|Df(v') − Df(v₁)|² + 2|Df(v') − Df(v₂)|² over v' ∈ Bⁿ_{s/2}((v₁ + v₂)/2) ⊆ Bⁿ_s(v₁) ∩ Bⁿ_s(v₂) gives |Df(v₁) − Df(v₂)| ≤ C₁₉(|v₁ − v₂|/σ₀)^{1/2}E₀^{1/2}.
8.8 C¹ regularity. Hence Df coincides Lⁿ-a.e. on A with a uniformly continuous map g (the continuous extension of Df restricted to the full-measure set of good points). As f is Lipschitz, its distributional derivative is Df; so the mollifications f_t := f ∗ ϱ_t satisfy Df_t = g ∗ ϱ_t → g locally uniformly on A and f_t → f uniformly. Therefore f is C¹ on A with Df = g, and ‖Df‖ ≤ Lip f ≤ L₀ ≤ ε on A.
8.9 Conclusion of (★). With δ = δ_A and γρ := σ₀/16 = δρ/16: by (9''), spt μ ∩ B̆_{γρ}(0) = F ∩ B̆_{γρ}(0); every x = Φ_f(v) ∈ F ∩ B̆_{γρ}(0) has |v| = |P x| < γρ, i.e. v ∈ A. Hence spt μ ∩ B̆_{γρ}(0) = Φ_f(A) ∩ B̆_{γρ}(0), with f(0) = 0, f C¹ on A and ‖Df‖ ≤ ε on A.

Part 9. The Lean statement.
Let δ_A ∈ (0, 1/8] be the minimum of δ₂ and the smallness conditions of 8.4; it depends only on n, k and ε (through L₀). Put δ₀ := δ_A and γ := δ_A/16 ∈ (0, 1]. Let U, W, R, H, κ, ρ, z satisfy the hypotheses. Then (SA) holds at the centre z with δ := δ₀: z ∈ spt μ, B_ρ(z) ⊆ W, μ(B_ρ(z)) ≤ (1 + δ₀)ω_nρⁿ, κρ ≤ δ₀ (and κ ≥ 0 since ‖H x‖ ≤ κ). Parts 2–8, centred at z, give T₀ and f. Let (a₁, …, aₙ) and (b₁, …, b_k) be orthonormal bases of T₀ and T₀^⊥, ι(v) := Σᵢ vᵢaᵢ, ι'(w) := Σ_j w_jb_j (linear isometries with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0), and u(v) := (⟨f(ιv), b_j⟩)_{j=1..k}, so ι'(u(v)) = f(ιv). Then z + ιv + ι'(u v) = z + Φ_f(ιv), u(0) = 0, u is C¹ on ball 0 (γρ) with ‖fderiv ℝ u v‖ = ‖Df(ιv)‖ ≤ ε there, and by 8.9, R.measure.support ∩ ball z (γρ) = ((fun v => z + ι v + ι' (u v)) '' ball 0 (γρ)) ∩ ball z (γρ).
proof_key_steps: x ↦ p_x is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (sibling tangent_projection_aesm, transferred from Hⁿ⌞M to μ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M), so every integral of p_x below is defined and R.firstVariation X = ∫ div_M X dμ.
Monotonicity inequalities (M1)/(M2) from the first variation with |H| ≤ κ (Simon Ch. 4, 3.17); hence Θ(μ, ·) exists, is upper semicontinuous and ≥ 1 on spt μ, Hⁿ(spt μ ∖ M) = 0 and θ ≤ Θ(μ, ·).
Density bounds ½ ≤ μ(B_t(y))/(ω_n tⁿ) ≤ 1 + Cδ and the radial tilt bound ∫|x−y|^{−n−2}|p_x^⊥(x−y)|² dμ ≤ Cδ at support points near z (Simon 2.4, enlarged range); θ = 1 a.e. near z.
Tilt bounded by height (Simon 2.1) and affine approximation (Simon 2.5) by a packing, Chebyshev and choice of a good tangent plane.
Lipschitz approximation and graph criterion (Simon 2.6–2.7) via the 5-times covering lemma, Lipschitz extension, and the monotonicity bound at points off the support (corrected radii).

Harmonic approximation with affine decay from the sibling harmonic_affine (Simon 3.1–3.4), applied to (C₁₃E₀)^{−1/2}fʲ, and tilt-excess decay E_*(ξ, θ₀σ, S) ≤ θ₀E_*(ξ, σ, T) with E_* = max{E, δ^{−1}κ²r²} (Simon 4.5–4.6, p = 2n).
Iteration of the decay at every point of spt μ near z gives E(ξ, s, S(ξ)) ≤ C(s/σ₀)E₀; the graph criterion makes spt μ ∩ B_{σ₀/8} the graph of f with Lip f ≤ L₀ ≤ ε.
Campanato estimate for Df gives f ∈ C^{1,1/2}; choosing orthonormal bases of T₀, T₀^⊥ yields ι, ι', u with u(0) = 0 and the graph identity on B_{γρ}(z), γ = δ₀/16.

subproblems.title: A cycle whose support is a C¹ graph near a support point is regular there (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let n ≥ 1, k ≥ 0, U ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} open, and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) represented by an integer multiplicity triple R = (M, θ, ξ) in U (T = τ(M, θ, ξ), R.Represents T), with ∂T = 0 in U. Let ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+k} and ι' : ℝ^k → ℝ^{n+k} be linear isometries with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 for all v, w; z ∈ ℝ^{n+k}; s, h > 0; and u : ℝⁿ → ℝ^k of class C¹ on the open ball B_s(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ with u(0) = 0. Put C := {z + ιv + ι'w : |v| < s, |w| < h} and Φ(v) := z + ιv + ι'u(v). If C ⊆ U, spt μ_R ∩ C = Φ(B_s(0)) (μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M = R.measure) and z ∈ spt T, then z ∈ reg T in the sense of the contract's regularSet: z ∈ spt T and there are ρ'' > 0 with B_{ρ''}(z) ⊆ U, m ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}, and an embedded C¹ n-submanifold Σ ∋ z with a continuous orientation ξ_Σ and Hⁿ(Σ ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ B_{ρ''}(z), such that T(ω) = m∫_Σ⟨ω, ξ_Σ⟩ dHⁿ for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ B_{ρ''}(z). (This is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dor_graph_supported_cycle_regular of DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.epsilon_regularity-a1.graph_cycle_regular-a1, reused here by exact name and frozen type.)

subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note: this child is the comparator-approved and independently reviewed declaration of DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.epsilon_regularity-a1.graph_cycle_regular-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 8a6855aa8803ff6f7de32b5a809497f6953347c4; its isolated comparator passed at 2026-10-13T04:14:36Z, lean-audit-v1 records comparator_passed = true, and its DAG record has been accepted since 2026-10-13T04:34:21Z), with character-identical frozen Lean type. No new proof work is required, and it has no DAG prerequisite. Its accepted natural-language proof follows verbatim. Here the word "parent" refers to that node's parent (the ε-regularity theorem of the other branch). It is used in step 7 of the sibling origin_regularity.
Source: steps 5–7 of the parent's supplied proof, i.e. the passage from Allard's graph conclusion to y ∈ reg T behind the book's 'Hence by Allard's Theorem 5.2 of Ch. 5 we have y ∈ reg T' in 7.4.3 (chapter-07.txt lines 624–631), together with the Constancy Theorem of Simon Ch. 6, 2.34 (chapter-06.txt lines 571–600), the area formula of Ch. 2, 3.2–3.5, the Upper Density Theorem of Ch. 1, 3.6 and Remark 3.7(2), and Ch. 3, 1.4–1.5 (approximate tangent planes). The parent's step 6 projects T⌞C to the base disc by Pr_# and applies 2.34 there; here the same argument is carried out directly on the integral representation of T (the projection Pr below plays the role of Pr_#, and the area formula replaces the push-forward formula 2.24(2)), because C¹ push-forward of currents is not in the library (only GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward). Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n] (it equals Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ and on n-planes); M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult (a positive integer on M), ξ := R.orient, μ := R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M; open balls are written B̆, closed balls B; D := B̆ⁿ_s(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ; e₁, …, eₙ is the standard basis of ℝⁿ; Φ(v) := z + ιv + ι'u(v); C := {z + ιv + ι'w : |v| < s, |w| < h}.

1. Orthogonal coordinates. Since ι, ι' are linear isometries with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0, the ranges L := ι(ℝⁿ) and L' := ι'(ℝ^k) are orthogonal subspaces of dimensions n and k, so ℝ^{n+k} = L ⊕ L'. Let ι*, ι'* be the adjoints: ι*ι = id, ι'*ι' = id, ι*ι' = 0, ι'*ι = 0 and ιι* + ι'ι'* = id. Put Pr(x) := ι*(x − z) ∈ ℝⁿ and Q(x) := ι'*(x − z) ∈ ℝ^k. These maps are affine, smooth and 1-Lipschitz, x = z + ιPr(x) + ι'Q(x) and |x − z|² = |Pr x|² + |Q x|². Hence C = {x : |Pr x| < s, |Q x| < h} is open. Φ is C¹ on D, Pr∘Φ = id and Q∘Φ = u; so Φ is injective and |Φ(v) − Φ(v')| ≥ |v − v'|. Put Σ := Φ(D).

2. Position of Σ. For v ∈ D, Φ(v) ∈ Φ(D) = spt μ ∩ C ⊆ C, so |u(v)| = |Q Φ(v)| < h. Thus Σ = spt μ ∩ C ⊆ C, Σ is relatively closed in C (spt μ is closed), and z = Φ(0) ∈ Σ because u(0) = 0.

3. Derivative and Jacobian. For v ∈ D, DΦ(v) = ι + ι'∘Du(v), so ι*∘DΦ(v) = id_{ℝⁿ}; DΦ(v) is injective with n-dimensional range L_v := DΦ(v)(ℝⁿ). By orthogonality DΦ(v)*DΦ(v) = I + Du(v)*Du(v), so JΦ(v) := (det DΦ(v)*DΦ(v))^{1/2} ≥ 1, and JΦ is continuous on D.

4. A smaller piece. Let s' := s/2, D' := B̆ⁿ_{s'}(0), Σ' := Φ(D'), C' := {x : |Pr x| < s', |Q x| < h} (open, Σ' ⊆ C' ⊆ C), and r'' := min{s', h}/2 > 0. The closed ball Bⁿ_{s'}(0) is a compact subset of D and Du is continuous on D, so Λ := max over Bⁿ_{s'}(0) of ‖Du‖ is finite and Φ is (1 + Λ)-Lipschitz on the convex set Bⁿ_{s'}(0). If |x − z| < r'' then |Pr x|, |Q x| ≤ |x − z| < r'', so B̆_{r''}(z) ⊆ C' ⊆ C ⊆ U.

5. Σ' is an embedded C¹ n-dimensional submanifold (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 n Σ'). For every y ∈ Σ' use the chart V := D', W := C', ψ := Φ: V and W are open; y ∈ W; Φ is C¹ on D' and injective; Φ(D') = Σ' = C' ∩ Σ' because Σ' ⊆ C'; fderiv Φ(v) = DΦ(v) is injective for v ∈ D' (step 3). Properness: let K ⊆ C' be compact. If |v| = s' then |Pr Φ(v)| = s', so Φ(v) ∉ C' ⊇ K. Hence D' ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) = Bⁿ_{s'}(0) ∩ Φ⁻¹(K), a closed subset (Φ is continuous on Bⁿ_{s'}(0) ⊆ D) of a compact set, hence compact.

6. Tangent spaces. Let y = Φ(v₀) ∈ Σ' with v₀ ∈ D'. Then tangentSpace Σ' y = L_{v₀}. (⊆) Let γ : ℝ → ℝ^{n+k} be C¹ on (−1, 1) with γ((−1,1)) ⊆ Σ', γ(0) = y and derivative w at 0. Since Φ(Pr x) = x for x ∈ Σ', γ(t) = Φ(Pr γ(t)) for |t| < 1; Pr∘γ takes values in D', is differentiable at 0 with derivative ι*w, and Φ is differentiable at v₀ = Pr γ(0). By the chain rule w = DΦ(v₀)(ι*w) ∈ L_{v₀}. (⊇) Given a ∈ ℝⁿ choose c > 0 with c|a| < s' − |v₀| and put γ(t) := Φ(v₀ + c·tanh(t/c)·a). Then v₀ + c tanh(t/c) a ∈ D' for all t, γ is C¹ on (−1, 1), γ((−1,1)) ⊆ Σ', γ(0) = y and γ'(0) = DΦ(v₀)a. Hence tangentSpace Σ' y is the n-dimensional subspace L_{v₀}.

7. Orientation. For v ∈ D let τ(v) = (τ₁(v), …, τₙ(v)) be the Gram–Schmidt orthonormalisation of (DΦ(v)e₁, …, DΦ(v)eₙ). It is an orthonormal basis of L_v and depends continuously on v (Gram–Schmidt is given by continuous formulas on linearly independent families, and v ↦ DΦ(v) is continuous on D). Define ξ_Σ : ℝ^{n+k} → MultiVector by ξ_Σ(x)(α) := α(τ(Pr x)) for x ∈ Σ and ξ_Σ(x) := 0 for x ∉ Σ.
 (a) For y ∈ Σ', IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_Σ y) L_{Pr y} holds, witnessed by τ(Pr y) with the + sign.
 (b) ξ_Σ is continuous on Σ, hence on Σ': x ↦ τ(Pr x) is continuous on Σ, and τ ↦ (α ↦ α(τ)) is continuous from (ℝ^{n+k})ⁿ into the dual of the covector space, since by multilinearity |α(τ) − α(τ')| ≤ ‖α‖ Σᵢ (∏_{j<i}|τ'_j|)|τᵢ − τ'ᵢ|(∏_{j>i}|τ_j|).
 With step 6 this gives IsOrientation n Σ' ξ_Σ.
 (c) Key identity: for v ∈ D and every n-covector α, α(DΦ(v)e₁, …, DΦ(v)eₙ) = JΦ(v)·ξ_Σ(Φ(v))(α). Indeed Gram–Schmidt gives DΦ(v)e_j = Σ_{i≤j} A_{ij} τᵢ(v) with A upper triangular and A_{jj} > 0, so α(DΦ(v)e₁, …, DΦ(v)eₙ) = det(A)·α(τ(v)) because α is multilinear and alternating; and DΦ(v)*DΦ(v) = AᵀA because τ(v) is orthonormal, so det A = JΦ(v).

8. Area formula and finiteness. For every t < s, Φ restricted to Bⁿ_t(0) is injective and Lipschitz with Jacobian JΦ, so (Simon Ch. 2, 3.2 and 3.5; library Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn, applied to a Lipschitz extension of Φ restricted to Bⁿ_t(0), and monotone convergence as t ↑ s): for every Borel A ⊆ D and Borel g ≥ 0, ∫_{Φ(A)} g dHⁿ = ∫_A g(Φ(v)) JΦ(v) dv, and likewise for g integrable over Φ(A). Consequences: (a) Hⁿ(Φ(A)) ≥ Lⁿ(A), so preimages under Φ of Hⁿ-null subsets of Σ are Lⁿ-null; (b) Hⁿ(Σ') ≤ (1 + Λ)ⁿ ω_n s'ⁿ < ∞ (LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le); (c) for compact K ⊆ C, K ∩ Σ = K ∩ spt μ is compact, so Pr(K ∩ Σ) is a compact subset of D, contained in some Bⁿ_t(0) with t < s, and Hⁿ(K ∩ Σ) < ∞.

9. μ is carried by Σ inside C. As ℝ^{n+k} is second countable, μ(ℝ^{n+k} ∖ spt μ) = 0 (MeasureTheory.Measure.measure_compl_support). Since spt μ ∩ C = Σ, μ(C ∖ Σ) = 0, and since θ ≥ 1 on M, Hⁿ((M ∩ C) ∖ Σ) = 0.

10. Approximate tangent planes of M on Σ. Claim: for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ C we have x ∈ Σ, and every subspace Q₀ with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q₀ equals L_{Pr x}.
 (a) Σ has approximate tangent plane L_{v₀} at every y = Φ(v₀) ∈ Σ. Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^{n+k}) with spt f ⊆ B_R(0). For small λ > 0 (λR < s − |v₀| and B_{λR}(y) ⊆ C), the points x ∈ Σ with |x − y| ≤ λR are of the form Φ(v) with |v − v₀| ≤ λR, because |Φ(v) − Φ(v₀)| ≥ |v − v₀|. By the scaling Hⁿ(λ·A) = λⁿHⁿ(A) and the area formula,
 ∫_{η_{y,λ}(Σ)} f dHⁿ = λ^{−n} ∫_Σ f((x − y)/λ) dHⁿ(x) = ∫_{|w| ≤ R} f((Φ(v₀ + λw) − Φ(v₀))/λ) JΦ(v₀ + λw) dw.
 The integrand is bounded by sup|f| · max over Bⁿ_{λR}(v₀) of JΦ, and converges for every w to f(DΦ(v₀)w) JΦ(v₀), since Φ is differentiable at v₀ and f, JΦ are continuous. By dominated convergence the limit is ∫_{ℝⁿ} f(DΦ(v₀)w) JΦ(v₀) dw = ∫_{L_{v₀}} f dHⁿ (area formula for the injective linear map DΦ(v₀), whose Jacobian is JΦ(v₀)). As dim L_{v₀} = n, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n Σ y L_{v₀}.
 (b) A := Σ ∖ M is Borel with Hⁿ(A ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ C (step 8(c)). By the Upper Density Theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6 with Remark 3.7(2), applied to Hⁿ⌞A in the open set C; library simon_theorem_3_6 and simon_remark_3_7_of_openSigmaFinite), the upper n-density of Hⁿ⌞A vanishes at Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ C ∖ A, in particular at Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ Σ.
 (c) Let x ∈ M ∩ Σ be such a point and let f, R be as in (a). For small λ with B_{λR}(x) ⊆ C,
 |∫_{η_{x,λ}(M)} f dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{x,λ}(Σ)} f dHⁿ| ≤ sup|f| · λ^{−n} (Hⁿ((M ∖ Σ) ∩ B_{λR}(x)) + Hⁿ(A ∩ B_{λR}(x))) = sup|f| · λ^{−n} Hⁿ(A ∩ B_{λR}(x)) → 0,
 using Hⁿ((M ∖ Σ) ∩ C) = 0 (step 9). So M has approximate tangent plane L_{Pr x} at x, and by uniqueness of approximate tangent planes (Simon Ch. 3, 1.5(1); HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), Q₀ = L_{Pr x}. Together with step 9 this proves the claim.

11. The orientation of R on Σ. By the IMRep field orients and step 10, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ C: x ∈ Σ and ξ(x)(α) = ±α(τ') for some orthonormal basis τ' of L_{Pr x}. Two orthonormal bases of the same n-dimensional space differ by an orthogonal matrix O, and α(τ') = det(O)·α(τ(Pr x)) with det O = ±1. Hence ξ(x) = ε(x)·ξ_Σ(x) with ε(x) ∈ {1, −1}. Let β(x) be the n-covector β(x)(w₁, …, wₙ) := det(⟨τᵢ(Pr x), w_j⟩)_{i,j}; it depends continuously on x ∈ Σ and β(x)(τ(Pr x)) = 1, so ε(x) = ξ(x)(β(x)). Define g : Σ → ℝ by g(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(β(x)) for x ∈ M ∩ Σ and g(x) := 0 for x ∈ Σ ∖ M. Then g is Hⁿ⌞Σ-measurable (ξ is a.e. strongly measurable, θ and β are measurable), |g| ≤ θ·1_M, g is integer-valued Hⁿ-a.e. on Σ, and θ(x)ξ(x) = g(x)ξ_Σ(x) for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ C.

12. Representation of T on C. Put G := g∘Φ on D.
 (a) G ∈ L¹_loc(D): for compact K' ⊆ D, Φ(K') is a compact subset of C ⊆ U, and ∫_{K'} |G| dv ≤ ∫_{K'} |G| JΦ dv = ∫_{Φ(K')} |g| dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M ∩ Φ(K')} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (IMRep.locallyIntegrable_mult).
 (b) G is Lⁿ-a.e. integer-valued on D (steps 11 and 8(a)).
 (c) For every ω ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω ⊆ C:
 T(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dHⁿ = ∫_{M ∩ C} θ ξ(ω) dHⁿ = ∫_Σ g ξ_Σ(ω) dHⁿ = ∫_D G(v) ω(Φ(v))(DΦ(v)e₁, …, DΦ(v)eₙ) dv.
 The first equality is R.Represents T; the second holds because ω = 0 off C; the third follows from steps 9 and 11 and g = 0 on Σ ∖ M; the fourth is the area formula (step 8) combined with the identity of step 7(c). All integrals converge: spt ω ∩ Σ is compact with finite Hⁿ-measure (step 8(c)), ω and ξ_Σ are bounded, and |g| ≤ θ·1_M is integrable on compact subsets of U.

13. ∂T = 0 gives zero weak derivatives of G. Write n = m + 1. Fix j ∈ {1, …, n} and a ∈ C_c^∞(D). The compact set u(spt a) lies in B̆^k_h(0) (step 2), so choose 0 < h₁ < h₂ < h with u(spt a) ⊆ B^k_{h₁}(0), and η ∈ C_c^∞(B̆^k_h(0)) with η ≡ 1 on B^k_{h₂}(0). Let ψ be the (n−1)-form on ℝⁿ given by ψ := (−1)^{j−1} a dv¹ ∧ ⋯ ∧ dv^{j−1} ∧ dv^{j+1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dvⁿ (for n = 1, ψ := a); then dψ = (∂_j a) dv¹ ∧ ⋯ ∧ dvⁿ, i.e. dψ(v)(e₁, …, eₙ) = ∂_j a(v). (With the library's normalisation of the exterior derivative this identity may carry a nonzero constant factor depending only on n and j; such a factor does not affect the conclusion ∫_D G ∂_j a dv = 0 below.) Define the (n−1)-form φ on ℝ^{n+k} by φ(x)(w₁, …, w_{n−1}) := η(Q x)·ψ(Pr x)(ι*w₁, …, ι*w_{n−1}), i.e. φ = (η∘Q)·Pr^#ψ with Pr^# the affine pull-back (library affinePullbackForm). Then φ is smooth with tsupport φ ⊆ z + ι(spt a) + ι'(spt η), a compact subset of C ⊆ U; so φ ∈ TestFormOn U m, and BoundaryVanishes T (T.boundary = 0) gives T(dφ) = 0.
 For v ∈ D: (i) if v ∉ spt a, the open set {x : Pr x ∉ spt a} contains Φ(v) and φ ≡ 0 on it, so dφ(Φ(v)) = 0 = ∂_j a(v); (ii) if v ∈ spt a, then |Q x| < h₂ on a neighbourhood of Φ(v) (as Q Φ(v) = u(v) ∈ B^k_{h₁}(0)), where φ = Pr^#ψ; exterior differentiation commutes with affine pull-back (Simon 6.1.14; library exteriorDerivative_affinePullbackForm), so dφ(Φ(v)) = (Pr^# dψ)(Φ(v)) and, using ι*∘DΦ(v) = id,
 dφ(Φ(v))(DΦ(v)e₁, …, DΦ(v)eₙ) = dψ(v)(ι*DΦ(v)e₁, …, ι*DΦ(v)eₙ) = dψ(v)(e₁, …, eₙ) = ∂_j a(v).
 Applying step 12(c) to ω := dφ (tsupport dφ ⊆ tsupport φ ⊆ C) gives
 0 = T(dφ) = ∫_D G(v) ∂_j a(v) dv for every a ∈ C_c^∞(D) and every j = 1, …, n.

14. Constancy. G ∈ L¹_loc(D), D is a connected open subset of ℝⁿ, and ∫_D G ∂_j a dv = 0 for all a ∈ C_c^∞(D) and all j. Hence there is c ∈ ℝ with G = c Lⁿ-a.e. on D. This is the argument of Simon Ch. 6, 2.34: the mollifications G_t := G ∗ ϱ_t are smooth on {v ∈ D : dist(v, ∂D) > t} with ∂_j G_t = 0 there (take a := ϱ_t(v − ·)), so G_t is constant on that ball, and G_t → G in L¹_loc(D). In the library: extend the identity to C¹ compactly supported a by mollifying a (∂_j(a ∗ ϱ_t) = (∂_j a) ∗ ϱ_t → ∂_j a uniformly, with supports in a fixed compact subset of D, while G is integrable there), then apply Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.ae_eq_const_of_weak_coordinate_derivatives_zero. Since G is Lⁿ-a.e. integer-valued (step 12(b)) and Lⁿ(D) > 0, c ∈ ℤ.

15. T = c[[Σ]] in C. For ω ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω ⊆ C, steps 12(c), 14, 7(c) and 8 give
 T(ω) = c ∫_D ω(Φ(v))(DΦ(v)e₁, …, DΦ(v)eₙ) dv = c ∫_Σ ξ_Σ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x).

16. c ≠ 0. Choose r > 0 with the closed ball B_r(z) ⊆ C (C is open and z ∈ C). If c = 0, step 15 gives T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω ⊆ B̆_r(z). The open set B̆_r(z) has compact closure B_r(z) ⊆ U, so it belongs to the family defining the zero region of T (GeometricCurrentOn.zeroRegion), hence z ∉ T.support — contradicting the hypothesis z ∈ T.support. So c ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}.

17. Conclusion z ∈ regularSet T. Take ρ := r'' (step 4), m := c, the manifold Σ' and the orientation ξ_Σ. Then: z ∈ T.support (hypothesis); r'' > 0 and ball z r'' ⊆ U (step 4); m ≠ 0 (step 16); z = Φ(0) ∈ Σ'; IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 n Σ' (step 5); IsOrientation n Σ' ξ_Σ (steps 6 and 7); for compact K ⊆ ball z r'', μHE[n](Σ' ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(Σ') < ∞ (step 8(b)); and for every ω ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω ⊆ ball z r'' (⊆ C' ⊆ C), step 15 gives T(ω) = c ∫_Σ ξ_Σ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) = c ∫_{Σ'} ξ_Σ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x), because every x = Φ(v) ∈ Σ ∖ Σ' has |x − z| ≥ |Pr x| = |v| ≥ s' > r'', so ω(x) = 0. These are exactly the defining conditions of z ∈ regularSet T.
proof_key_steps: Orthogonal coordinates Pr = ι*(· − z), Q = ι'*(· − z): C is open and Σ := Φ(B_s(0)) = spt μ ∩ C is an injective C¹ graph through z.
Σ' := Φ(B_{s/2}(0)) is an embedded C¹ n-submanifold with tangentSpace = DΦ(ℝⁿ), Gram–Schmidt orientation ξ_Σ (continuous) and finite Hⁿ-measure; α(DΦe₁,…,DΦeₙ) = JΦ·ξ_Σ(α).
μ(C ∖ Σ) = 0; by the area formula and the upper density theorem the approximate tangent plane of M equals T_xΣ a.e. on M ∩ C, so θξ = gξ_Σ with g integer-valued.
Representation T(ω) = ∫_D G(v) ω(Φ(v))(DΦ(v)e₁,…,DΦ(v)eₙ) dv on C with G = g∘Φ ∈ L¹_loc(D).
Testing ∂T = 0 with φ = (η∘Q)·Pr^#ψ gives ∫_D G ∂_j a = 0 for all a ∈ C_c^∞(D); distributional constancy (Simon 6.2.34) gives G ≡ c ∈ ℤ a.e.
T = c[[Σ]] on C, c ≠ 0 because z ∈ spt T; restricting to Σ' and the ball B_{r''}(z) gives z ∈ regularSet T.

subproblems.title: ε-regularity at the origin for minimizing currents in ℝ^P (Allard 5.2 via Simon 7.1.2)
subproblems.statement: Let P, j ∈ ℕ with 1 ≤ j ≤ P. Then there is a real δ > 0 with the following property. Let C ∈ 𝒟_j(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) j) be minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn C univ, Simon 7.1.1; in particular C is integer multiplicity), with ∂C = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C) and 0 ∈ spt C (C.support), and suppose M_{B_ρ(0)}(C) ≤ (1 + δ)·ω_j·ρ^j in [0, ∞] for every real ρ with 0 < ρ ≤ 1, i.e. C.massOn (ball 0 ρ) ≤ ofReal(1 + δ)·unitBallVolume j·ofReal(ρ^j); here B_ρ(0) is the open ball, M_W = massOn (Simon 6.2.5) and ω_j = unitBallVolume j is the Lebesgue measure of the unit ball of ℝ^j. Then 0 ∈ reg C (regularSet C, Simon 7.4.1 as in the contract: 0 ∈ spt C and there are ρ' > 0, m ∈ ℤ ∖ {0} and an embedded oriented C¹ j-submanifold M ∋ 0 of locally finite Hʲ-measure in B_{ρ'}(0) with C = m[[M]] in B_{ρ'}(0)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → j ≤ P → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) j, IsMinimizingIn C univ → BoundaryVanishes C → (0 : Euclid P) ∈ C.support → (∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ρ ≤ 1 → C.massOn (ball 0 ρ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (1 + δ) * unitBallVolume j * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ j)) → (0 : Euclid P) ∈ regularSet C
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 7, Lemma 1.2 (minimizing currents are stationary; chapter-07.txt lines 29–60), here in the flat case N = ℝ^P, followed by Allard's Regularity Theorem (Ch. 5, 5.2; chapter-05.txt lines 1008–1032) applied at the origin. This is how the book itself uses them in 7.4.3 (chapter-07.txt lines 626–631: "by Allard's Theorem 5.2 of Ch. 5 we have y ∈ reg T … (1.2 justifies the use of 5.2 of Ch. 5)") and in the proof of 7.4.4(8) (lines 673–675).
Every analytic input is a sibling of this decomposition. E and K are comparator-accepted declarations, reused by exact name and type; F, G and J are siblings declared under fresh names; no unaccepted declaration of another DAG branch is used:
- E = imrep_mass_support (Submission.dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support, comparator-accepted);
- F = c1_pushforward (Submission.dimred_cdg_c1_diffeo_pushforward_im);
- G = first_variation_bound (Submission.dimred_cdg_pushforward_massOn_le_first_variation);
- J = allard_graph (Submission.dimred_cdg_allard_bounded_curvature_graph);
- K = graph_cycle_regular (Submission.dor_graph_supported_cycle_regular, comparator-accepted).
Notation: for R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep, μ := R.measure = θH^j⌞M and δV(X) := R.firstVariation X = ∫_M θ div_M X dH^j. B_r(x) is the open ball (Lean ball) and B̄_r(x) the closed ball; spt X := tsupport X; ω_j := unitBallVolume j; M_W := massOn; spt C := C.support.
1. (Dimensions and constants.) Since j ≤ P, write P = j + k with k := P − j (in Lean: obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le), so ℝ^P is literally Euclid (j + k). Apply J with n := j ≥ 1, this k and ε := 1/4. It yields δ₀ > 0 and γ ∈ (0, 1], depending only on j and k, i.e. only on P and j. Put δ := δ₀ > 0. This δ is fixed before C is chosen, as the statement requires.
2. (Representation, mass and support.) Let C satisfy the hypotheses for this δ. IsMinimizingIn C univ contains IsIntegerMultiplicity C, so there is R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep univ j with R.Represents C. Apply E with U := ℝ^P (open), T := C and R:
- (E1) M_W(C) = μ(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P;
- (E2) spt C = ℝ^P ∩ spt μ = spt μ.
Since 0 ∈ spt C by hypothesis, 0 ∈ spt μ.
3. (Stationarity: δV(X) = 0 for every C¹ vector field X : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with compact support.) This is Simon 7.1.2 for N = ℝ^P. Fix such an X and put K := spt X, a compact set.
 3.1 DX is continuous with compact support, so A := sup_x ‖DX(x)‖ is finite, and A ≥ 0. By the mean value inequality on the convex set ℝ^P, |X(x) − X(y)| ≤ A|x − y| for all x, y.
 3.2 For t ∈ ℝ let φ_t(y) := y + tX(y). Each φ_t is C¹. φ_t = id outside K, since X = 0 there. Dφ_t(x) = I + tDX(x), so ‖Dφ_t(x) − I − tDX(x)‖ = 0 ≤ ε|t| for all ε > 0, t and x.
 3.3 Let |t|A < 1.
 (a) φ_t is injective: φ_t(x) = φ_t(y) gives x − y = t(X(y) − X(x)), so |x − y| ≤ |t|A|x − y|, whence x = y.
 (b) φ_t is surjective: |(φ_t(x) − φ_t(y)) − (x − y)| = |t||X(x) − X(y)| ≤ |t|A|x − y|. So φ_t approximates the identity isomorphism of ℝ^P on all of ℝ^P with constant |t|A < 1 = ‖id⁻¹‖⁻¹, and φ_t is onto by Mathlib's ApproximatesLinearOn.surjective with f' = ContinuousLinearEquiv.refl. For P = 0 the space is a single point. Equivalently, for each y the map x ↦ y − tX(x) is a contraction of the complete space ℝ^P, and its fixed point x satisfies φ_t(x) = y.
 (c) Dφ_t(x) is injective for every x: (I + tDX(x))v = 0 gives |v| = |t||DX(x)v| ≤ |t|A|v|, so v = 0.
 (d) φ_t(K) ⊆ K: if x ∈ K and φ_t(x) ∉ K, then φ_t(φ_t(x)) = φ_t(x) because φ_t = id off K. By (a), φ_t(x) = x, which contradicts x ∈ K.
 3.4 (The open set W.) Let K' := K ∪ {0}, a compact set, and W := {y : dist(y, K') < 1}, an open set.
- K ⊆ W and B_1(0) ⊆ W.
- closure(W) ⊆ {y : dist(y, K') ≤ 1}, which is compact because ℝ^P is proper. Hence W ⊂⊂ ℝ^P (CompactlyContained W univ).
- μ is finite on compact sets: for compact Q, μ(Q) = ∫_{M∩Q} θ dH^j < ∞ by IMRep.locallyIntegrable_mult (via withDensity_apply and Measure.restrict_restrict). So μ(W) ≤ μ({dist(·, K') ≤ 1}) < ∞.
- μ(W) ≥ μ(B_1(0)) > 0, because 0 ∈ spt μ (step 2).
Put m := μ(W) ∈ (0, ∞).
 3.5 (First-variation bound.) G applies with U := ℝ^P, this W, R, X and the family φ. Its hypotheses hold: W is open; μ(W) ≠ ∞; X is C¹ with compact support; spt X = K ⊆ W; every φ_t is C¹ and equals the identity off spt X; and the derivative condition holds by 3.2. Hence for every ε > 0 there is δ_G > 0 with the following property. For every |t| < δ_G and every S ∈ 𝒟_j(ℝ^P) with S(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(φ_t x)∘Dφ_t(x)) dH^j(x) for all ω ∈ 𝒟^j(ℝ^P), we have M_W(S) ≤ ofReal(m + t·δV(X) + ε|t|).
 3.6 (Choice of t.) Suppose a := δV(X) ≠ 0. Take ε := |a|/2 and δ_G from 3.5. Put s := min{δ_G/2, 1/(2(A + 1)), m/|a|} > 0, and t := −s if a > 0, t := s if a < 0. Then:
- |t| = s < δ_G and |t|A < 1;
- ta = −s|a|;
- 0 < s|a| ≤ m.
 3.7 (The competitor.) F applies with U := ℝ^P (open), K, T := C, R and φ := φ_t. Its hypotheses hold: R represents C; K is compact; and φ_t is C¹, bijective, has injective derivative everywhere and equals the identity off K (3.2–3.3). It gives an integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟_j(ℝ^P) with ∂S = 0 (because ∂C = 0) and S(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω(φ_t x)∘Dφ_t(x)) dH^j for all ω.
 3.8 (spt(S − C) ⊆ K.) Let y ∉ K and choose r > 0 with B_r(y) ∩ K = ∅ (K is closed). Let ω ∈ 𝒟^j(ℝ^P) with spt ω ⊆ B_r(y). Using C(ω) = R.action(ω), (S − C)(ω) = S(ω) − C(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)[ξ(x)(ω(φ_t x)∘Dφ_t(x)) − ξ(x)(ω(x))] dH^j(x). The two integrands coincide at every x:
- if x ∈ K, then φ_t(x) ∈ K by 3.3(d), so ω(φ_t x) = 0 = ω(x), since ω vanishes off B_r(y) and B_r(y) misses K;
- if x ∉ K, then φ_t = id on the open neighbourhood ℝ^P ∖ K of x, so φ_t(x) = x and Dφ_t(x) = I.
Hence S − C vanishes on B_r(y), an open set with compact closure in ℝ^P. So y lies in the zero region of S − C, and y ∉ spt(S − C). Thus spt(S − C) ⊆ K. Since spt(S − C) is closed (the complement of the open zero region) and K is compact, spt(S − C) is compact. Also spt(S − C) ⊆ K ⊆ ℝ^P ∩ W.
 3.9 (Minimality.) The competitor S is admissible in Simon 7.1.1:
- ∂S = ∂C, both being 0 (j ≥ 1);
- S is integer multiplicity;
- W is open with W ⊂⊂ ℝ^P;
- spt(S − C) is a compact subset of ℝ^P ∩ W.
So IsMinimizingIn C univ gives M_W(C) ≤ M_W(S). By (E1), M_W(C) = μ(W) = ofReal(m). By 3.5–3.6, M_W(S) ≤ ofReal(m + ta + (|a|/2)|t|) = ofReal(m − s|a|/2). Since 0 < m − s|a|/2 < m, we get ofReal(m − s|a|/2) < ofReal(m), a contradiction. Hence δV(X) = 0.
4. (Closed-ball mass bound.) For ρ ∈ (1/2, 1], B̄_{1/2}(0) ⊆ B_ρ(0). By (E1) and the hypothesis of the statement, μ(B̄_{1/2}(0)) ≤ μ(B_ρ(0)) = M_{B_ρ(0)}(C) ≤ (1 + δ₀)ω_jρ^j. The right side is continuous in ρ, with a finite value at ρ = 1/2 because ω_j < ∞. Letting ρ ↓ 1/2 gives μ(B̄_{1/2}(0)) ≤ (1 + δ₀)ω_j(1/2)^j.
5. (Allard at the origin.) Apply J, with the δ₀ and γ of step 1, to U := W := ℝ^P, R, H :≡ 0, κ := 0, ρ := 1/2 and z := 0. Its hypotheses hold:
- W is open and W ⊆ U;
- B̄_{1/2}(0) ⊆ W;
- H is measurable with |H| ≤ κ = 0;
- for every C¹ compactly supported X, δV(X) = 0 = −∫⟨X, H⟩ dμ (step 3);
- 0 ∈ spt μ (step 2);
- μ(B̄_{1/2}(0)) ≤ (1 + δ₀)ω_j(1/2)^j (step 4);
- κρ = 0 ≤ δ₀.
Put r := γ/2 > 0. J gives:
- linear isometries ι : ℝ^j → ℝ^P and ι' : ℝ^k → ℝ^P with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 for all v, w;
- u : ℝ^j → ℝ^k with u(0) = 0, u of class C¹ on B_r(0) ⊆ ℝ^j and ‖Du(v)‖ ≤ 1/4 there;
- spt μ ∩ B_r(0) = Φ(B_r(0)) ∩ B_r(0), where Φ(v) := 0 + ιv + ι'u(v).
6. (The graph over a cylinder.) Put σ := r/4 > 0 and Cyl := {0 + ιv + ι'w : |v| < σ, |w| < σ}.
 6.1 For v ∈ B_r(0), |u(v)| ≤ |v|/4. Indeed u is differentiable at every point of the open convex ball B_r(0), being C¹ there, with ‖Du‖ ≤ 1/4. So the mean value inequality gives |u(v) − u(0)| ≤ |v − 0|/4, and u(0) = 0.
 6.2 |ιv + ι'w| ≤ |ιv| + |ι'w| = |v| + |w|. Hence Cyl ⊆ B_{2σ}(0) ⊆ B_r(0).
 6.3 If ιv + ι'w = ιv' + ι'w', then v = v' and w = w'. Indeed ι(v − v') = ι'(w' − w), so |ι(v − v')|² = ⟨ι(v − v'), ι'(w' − w)⟩ = 0. Hence |v − v'| = |ι(v − v')| = 0. Then ι'w = ι'w', and ι' is injective.
 6.4 spt μ ∩ Cyl = Φ(B_σ(0)).
- (⊆) Let x = ιv + ι'w ∈ spt μ with |v|, |w| < σ. By 6.2, x ∈ B_r(0), so by step 5, x = Φ(v') for some v' ∈ B_r(0). By 6.3, v' = v and w = u(v). So x = Φ(v) with v ∈ B_σ(0).
- (⊇) Let |v| < σ. By 6.1, |u(v)| ≤ |v|/4 < σ, so Φ(v) ∈ Cyl ⊆ B_r(0). Also v ∈ B_r(0). So Φ(v) ∈ Φ(B_r(0)) ∩ B_r(0) = spt μ ∩ B_r(0) by step 5.
7. (Regularity.) Apply K with n := j ≥ 1, k, U := ℝ^P (open), T := C, R, ι, ι', u, z := 0 and s := h := σ. Its hypotheses hold:
- R represents C, and ∂C = 0;
- ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 for all v, w, and σ > 0;
- u is C¹ on B_σ(0) ⊆ B_r(0), and u(0) = 0;
- Cyl ⊆ ℝ^P, and spt μ ∩ Cyl = Φ(B_σ(0)) (6.4);
- 0 ∈ spt C.
Hence 0 ∈ reg C (regularSet C). ∎

- 3.3: ApproximatesLinearOn.surjective with ContinuousLinearEquiv.refl and ContinuousLinearMap.nnnorm_id; the Subsingleton case covers P = 0.

- 3.8: the zero region is witnessed by ball y r with isCompact_closedBall and closure_ball_subset_closedBall; fderiv_of_notMem_tsupport gives DX = 0, hence Dφ_t = I, off K.
- 3.9: ENNReal.ofReal_lt_ofReal_iff.
- 4: ge_of_tendsto, Ioo_mem_nhdsGT and ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul.
- 6: LinearIsometry.norm_map, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, sub_eq_sub_iff_add_eq_add, add_left_cancel and LinearIsometry.injective.
proof_key_steps: Write P = j + k and take δ := δ₀ from the sibling allard_graph with n = j and ε = 1/4; δ₀ and γ depend only on (P, j).
A minimizing C has an integer multiplicity representation R; the sibling imrep_mass_support gives M_W(C) = μ_R(W) for open W and spt C = spt μ_R, so 0 ∈ spt μ_R.

Flat Simon 7.1.2: for X ∈ C¹_c, φ_t = id + tX is a C¹ bijection with injective derivative for |t|·sup‖DX‖ < 1. The sibling c1_pushforward gives integer multiplicity competitors S_t with spt(S_t − C) ⊆ spt X. Minimality on W ⊃ spt X ∪ B_1(0), with M_W(C) = μ(W) > 0, combined with the sibling first_variation_bound, forces δV(X) = 0.
The open-ball mass hypothesis on (1/2, 1] gives μ(B̄_{1/2}(0)) ≤ (1 + δ₀)ω_j(1/2)^j in the limit.
The sibling allard_graph, applied with H ≡ 0, κ = 0, ρ = 1/2 and z = 0, makes spt μ near 0 the graph of a C¹ map u with u(0) = 0 and |Du| ≤ 1/4.
Orthogonality of ι and ι' and |u(v)| ≤ |v|/4 identify spt μ in the cylinder of radius γ/8 with the graph; the sibling graph_cycle_regular then gives 0 ∈ reg C.
